review_text: I have lived in Bankier's apartments for the past two years and have had a great experience in specifically the 1107 S Second St. apartments (Roundbalconies). The maintenance on campus is fantastic. Any time I sent in a maintenance request, I was serviced within two business days at the latest. The apartment was fully furnished (~40 in wide screen T.V, brand new couches, beds, and kitchen table). The staff that works in the main building are all very accommodating to your needs and I have worked with them on numerous occasions. Unfortunately I am moving out but the Roundbalcony apartments are all being refurnished and are a steal. The price, location, and value for your dollar is top class here. Only setback is that electricity bill can be a bit steep in the winter (due to heating) but the price you pay for rent offsets that. As well, almost all apartments on campus have this issue regardless. Best deal on campus that not many have heard about. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Bankier is really the most top-notch leasing group in Champaign Urbana for us folks who can't afford to live in the brand new high rises that are springing up all over the place. When I was viewing units at the start of their leasing season, Keith showed me a unit that was in the process of being remodeled after I shot down everything else he had to offer. Even though it was half painted and didn't even have cabinets yet, I was enamored with the space. Naturally, I had a million questions for Keith, and I was surprised to find that he confidently had answers for most of them.

Things that he didn't have answers for (will it have a garbage disposal? can I get it unfurnished? do you HAVE to paint these gorgeous hardwood beams or can we leave them exposed?), he made some calls and found out. At most places this probably would have been a weeks-long ordeal to get sorted, and Keith got me the info I needed before we even left the unit.

I signed shortly after, and that was about 8 months before the lease started. During that period, Keith never batted an eye when I hit him with off the wall questions directly via email, and was even so kind as to give me some progress shots of the remodel, as well as a handful of images of the finished product. He was very responsive all the way up until move in day.

The move in process was as smooth as any on campus. There were a few items that needed attention in the unit, which was to be expected. I drafted up my maintenance requests, sent them to Keith, and he submitted them on my behalf shortly afterward. He also helped me get moved in early, which made life so much easier. I've been in the new place a few weeks now, and it's really quite nice. My requests have been taken care of, Keith is still as responsive as ever, and has even offered to drop in and help me with some things like wall mounting my TV. Overall, I'm a very happy tenant!

review_text:
I live in bankier's apt for over three years, and I would like to give a fair review for other UI students.
Pro:
Location Location Location!: most of their apts locate in the center of Champaign downtown, which is extremely convenient for students work in lab till late night and need food around.
Payment option: This company accept check/online bank transfer/ credit card to pay rent, which is convenient.
Space: Their room tend to be larger than market average.
Rooms available even if you apply late: Better apts generally runs out pretty quick, Hot apts could get out of space for next two to three years!

Con:
Obsolete building: Most of their building were really old. They do maintenance, but problems still occur frequently. For example, water heater in upper unit exploded and huge amount of water flood my belongings. You will need to take all these losses by yourself without renter's insurance. (generally cost +$100/Mo.) Heating/Cooling cost is high due to lack of Insulation.

Noise: If you live in their old building, then you will hear every single detail of what your neighbor does. Such as they fart in toilet, close the door, make Love, say something to themselves, & etc...

Overpriced: Bankier's apts generally tend to give slightly higher price compare to others. If your budget is tight, then choice other apts.

Landlord entre your room frequently: Urbana city require landlord give notice at least one day before they enter your room. However, Champaign does not have such law. Although most of the time, landlord will knock the door before they open your door. There are several times that staff open my door without any notice. Live in Urbana if you really care about privacy.

Overcharging: It is quite often that they charge you for problem that exist when you move in. They refuse to fix those problem and then charge $$$$ for that when you move out. The company also refuse renter to steam clean the carpet by themselves. (If you do so they still charge you carpet clean fee) Therefore, you will have hundreds more bill when moving out compare to other companies. MAKE SURE YOU TAKE PHOTO OF EVERYTHING WHEN YOU MOVE IN&OUT!!! PHOTOCOPY THE CONDITION LIST SHEET before you turn it in.

Dishonesty: Their mouths were full of lies toward international student, and I am not the only victim of their lie. It's quite often that they lie about condition of apts when they *talk* about the room. So you must VISIT THE EXACT ROOM YOU WILL LIVE IN BEFORE YOU SIGN THE LEASE.  Misleading information include mail/package/parking. Take your time read the lease documents! Again, you must visit the exact room!

PS: all these cons were true for old apts, if you live in their new building (e.g. Skyline Tower), then the only problem is overprice.

In summary: Live in Bankier's old build will give you an average to below average experience. (3 to 2 star) Their new building should give you a good to excellent experience. (4 to 5 star).

Others: C-U area generally tend to be very safe (compare to Chicago downtown, & etc...), and this area does not have bed bug problem too. Most of apts are roach free (or the pest control work really well). Most of downtown apts are furnished with acceptable price. TAKE THE COURSE GIVEN BY UOFI TENANT UNION BEFORE YOU MAKE DECISION!!!

Not only were they able to accommodate my short initial move-in request early in spring but since then they've been nothing but professional and exceptional in customer service support. My unit is beautiful and modern and very well maintained. One day my key fob didn't work on the buildings new security system, MHM literally had someone meet me at the property around 530am and stayed here until the building security team corrected the problem. My refrigerator broke down, again someone came that evening with A TEMPORARY REPLACEMENT 😳🤯. I WAS AMAZED!  Every issue I've had, cause things happen, has been met with immediate response from MHM where I was given a time and day for immediate resolution. MHM has been absolutely phenomenal. I am very happy I ended up with them. MHM understands that I got too many other things to worry about...the place I call home should not be one of them.

I have lived with MHM for nearly a year now and I have had a good experience with them.
The location is very competitively priced for a single person apartment close to campus.

Issues that I have had in terms of maintenance and such were often resolved the same day, and smaller things like replacing old furniture has often been handled with in a week.

I have mainly interacted with Chris from maintenance and Kevin from the office, and both have been very helpful, responsive, and kind. In my experience they have gone above and beyond to make living here enjoyable and I am very happy with my interactions with them.

I just wish I knew about MHM Properties earlier. I have lived in two separate MHM apartments and I could not think of any complaints. The maintenance team is always quick, management team is kind, and the buildings are well maintained. Living space affects your life; MHM apartments made my life in Champaign so pleasant and I wish more leasing companies in Urbana-Champaign were as kind and honest as the MHM Properties. I miss the MHM apartment I lived now that I moved out. It was a great place with lots of sun lights, space, and location for a reasonable price! I sincerely wish MHM Properties the best and hopefully more students choose MHM over other leasing companies.

Overall, I had a great experience leasing with MHM.
All of my maintenance requests were promptly resolved during the initial move-in as well as throughout the course of the lease. The team even went above and beyond to coordinate with Volo to rewire and upgrade the entire building's internet after I put in a request, with no additional costs to me.
Pricing for both the apartment as well as parking were very reasonable. Electricity and water were billed separately by Ameren and American Water, respectively, but everything else was included.
My apartment was only shown about 7 times throughout the course of the lease (mostly grouped towards the first few months), and I always received at least a day's notice. Most of the showings lasted only a few minutes and were all at reasonable times.
At the end of my lease, nearly my entire security deposit was returned minus a small charge for mandatory carpet cleaning, which they disclosed up-front in the lease. No other BS painting or cleaning fees were charged.

I have lived with MHM properties in two separate locations throughout my undergraduate and graduate degrees and could not have asked for a better property manager. Kevin and his team are incredibly responsive, kind-hearted, and willing to make your living experience as simple as possible. The maintenance is top-notch, they have locations across campus for housing and parking, and their online system is simple and effective.

Routine maintenance such such as furnace filters, common area cleaning (stairwells, landings), etc. is done frequently and with advanced notice. Their online portal allows tenants to make maintenance requests without needing to call or email, and the maintenance team typically addresses the issue within 24-hours or less. I've never encountered any "emergency" maintenance issues, but I'm fully confident they would respond as soon as possible if that were ever the case.

All of the units (even in the older buildings where I have lived) are kept in good condition, and are sprinkled in great locations across campus. Most of their units also have parking, many times covered parking which is great for the winter months and I was so happy to have when I began working off-campus and drove everyday. If you own and use your car, the comparatively low monthly charge for parking is definitely worth the cost. You will pay for utilities such as power and water, however internet is covered by MHM. This is something you should look for around here as large companies like comcast have employed somewhat predatory marketing schemes to trap local students into exorbitant internet prices. Internet speeds provided by MHM are fast and reliable, even during 2020-2021 when many more people were at home all day using their bandwidth to its fullest extent. Very happy with the internet quality to say the least. Trash pick up, sewage, and other city related costs are all taken care of by MHM. Cost of keeping the outdoor areas clean is also taken care of; most notably, MHM always salts their building's walk ways for the winter months ahead of snow storms. This should be a standard, however many property management companies around here fail to do it. MHM has never let me down on this. Every year, if there is snow, there is salt in front of all the doors. This is a great way to keep tenants as they wont be cracking their skulls on the concrete and dropping out of school. MHM is truly onto something here, great work.

Finally, their online portal for rent payments, lease agreements, maintenance requests and rent applications is incredible. All payments are made online through their application. It is safe, effective, and highly convenient. I have not seen a property management portal that surpasses it. Cost of the rent itself is also very reasonable, especially when you consider the cost of a similar location and unit, MHM has consistently been fairly priced for the 7 years I have lived with them. Rent will go up by maybe $5 a year per person in the unit and can typically be tracked by the rising city costs (sewage, property tax, etc.), incredibly fair and affordable by my standards.

MHM is reliable, consistent, has all the necessary amenities to make your living situation simple, and are just all around good people. My friends and coworkers all have horror stories about their living situations that I cannot relate to. MHM has been incredible from day 1, to year 7. I was referred by an acquaintance I met on a Peoria Charter bus, and so I am leaving this review to hopefully encourage other people to skip all the stress of finding a place to live, nit-picking lease agreements, fighting with the landlords over every bit of maintenance, and just go ahead and give Kevin a call. review_text:

Special shout-out to Kurt who helped me get the apartment and answered all of my emails timely without any hesitation.

Thank you again,
Aylin

Best realtor for university students studying at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. I stayed at 909 S 1st Street from January to July in a studio apartment. I had the best experience and response in terms of maintenance requests. The staff is very welcoming and responsive. Special shoutout to Kurt who helped me get the apartment in the easiest way I could ever imagine. As an international student, my experience was worth every penny! Would definitely recommend this place to students looking for semester or annual leases.

Best,
Suprit

I was able to do a semester rental with Roland Realty and it was a very smooth process. Communicated with Thomas and Kurt mainly and they are, along with management and maintenance, very friendly and responsive. Thanks!

My son was able to rent an apartment for only 5 months (semester rental).  It was a reasonable rate, and the building was solid.  Lots of realtors charge massive $$ off your deposit.  But Roland did it right, and only charged us some minor misc fees for areas we didn't clean when moving out (e.g.- top of refrigerator, under seat cushions).  Roland is way better then some other area realtor we had used the prior year.

Overall a great apartment at this price, maintenance is responsive, walls are not thin, area is safe.
Two things I don’t like: they constantly show my unit to perspective tenants without any notification, knock the door and open if you don’t answer within 5 seconds. The pool opens for public, people play loud music all day long, kinda annoying especially when you want to take a nap

Please do yourself a favor and DO NOT lease with Roland. It’s an entire scam and they just want your money!! The process of finding an apartment with them started out great. Extremely friendly staff and the process was easy and smooth. Yet, they “claim” to cover a certain amount of your utilities. It is all a lie!! The amount I paid for ONE month was extremely ridiculous. Even better, they don’t send your utility bill each month... they wait to give it to you like 3 months after. How unprofessional is that? Please please please do not sublease here unless you honestly want your money STOLEN. You will NEVER see a cent of your security deposit back. They charge you for having dust on your drawers and every little thing possible. This is a total robbery and criminal. I beg you to not lease with them and if you are already, well good luck.

The apartment was also infested with WASPS!!  It was a beautiful apartment and spacious for 2 people. One of my roommates who subleased first semester had found wasps and immediately called Roland so they can contact pest control. They came in and told us it was “horse flies”, clearly it wasn’t. It took them 3-4 times to come into our apartment to finally determine that it was wasps. Better yet, my roommate was living in constant fear because she’s deadly allergic to all types of bees.

Please do not lease here!

I lived at 907 S 2nd for my final year at UIUC and the Roland staff were nothing short of friendly and helpful. Maintenance requests were fulfilled quickly and the leasing staff office was great! My studio had normal wear and tear expected of a college apartment building, but the noise from people going to their upstairs apartments and thin walls got a little frustrating while trying to study. Simple move out process/key return as well! I will update my review once I receive my security deposit to let others know possible fees to expect.

I had a very pleasant experience with Roland Realty, especially with Kurt, the apartment manager!! Kurt is a very understanding/reasonable guy who genuinely cares for the well-being of his future tenants. It was my first time signing a contract to an apartment so naturally, I was nervous. I had heard many stories about other apartments taking advantage of students because they didn't know any better. However, Kurt helped me every step of the way & boy am I grateful to have had such an awesome manager! I recommend Roland Realty to anyone 10/10 :-)

Edit: I’m lowering the stars. After over a year of living in an adequate apartment I’m now realizing how bad my old apartment at Roland was as that was my first apartment ever. They literally sold me an apartment with severe mold issues & inadequate heating & cooling. Horrible. Had I continued to say in the apartment I would have gotten severely sick. Please do not rent an apartment with Roland if it is at basement level. I’m sure the experience was better at higher floors.

I stayed at the mid-tier Roland Realty apartment on the basement level and it was exactly that. Advertised as full renovation but it was clear the whole apartment & building wasn’t renovated well because of the severe issues. Severe mold issues, basement stench, the hallways also had mold issues, never cleaned, cobwebs, mud & dirt always caked to the stairs, inadequate heating and cooling especially for the basement apartment. There was only one little box vent to heat the entire apartment and the heat never adequately reached the bedroom and bathroom area.

The apartment had severe black mold issues. Black mold was literally growing on the walls and floor. I left my apartment in late May 2020 to visit family and when I came back in June 2020 all my clothes and shoes that were touching the floor and walls ended up coated in mold. The daily cleaning of my apartment I did was the only thing that kept the mold at bay. But obviously when I left for a month, the severity of the mold took over. I had only been in that apartment for 6 months total from the beginning of the lease to the end so the severe mold issues were not because of me.

Roland Realty does not upkeep their properties well.
In my building there was always trash all over the ground & sidewalks in the back of the building. Since my window was on the basement level, there was trash all in front of my window. Dirt was caked to my windows as well.The outdated air conditioner they provided was coated in mold from the outside and filthy as it was at ground level.

Roland Realty was the best apartment company I leased with during my time at University of Illinois. They were always friendly when I went to pick up packages or ask them a question. They even got to know me by name, which definitely made Roland apartments feel like home.
They responded quickly to maintenance requests. The maintenance people were friendly. I lived in a complex that had free TV, water, and laundry downstairs... can't get much better than that. They also were relatively fair in returning the security deposit.

A good apartment complex in seniorland. And they had their own pool!
Found cockroaches in the walls and blood stains on the carpets. DO NOT RENT OUT HERE.

Terrible company.  Our apartment (907.5 S. Oak) had several issues that needed to be fixed by maintenance, and we followed the correct procedure in requesting that they be fixed.  Roland consistently blew us off for months after several complaints.  The lot next door was under construction, and our private driveway was constantly used and blocked off by another realty company, to which Roland showed no concern.  This company does not give a damn about their customers, they only care about collecting overpriced rent checks.

They would have gotten 5 stars from me only if they provided their tenants with advance notice before showing the apartments to prospective tenants (and my first comment did not got deleted mysteriously.)

This was before covid so not sure how things are, but my experience was not pleasant. They will request to come in to show the prospective apartments the place without sending any advance notice. If you don't hear the door, they will enter in. If you hear the door, then you can say "no" to their request and they will be fine with it, but it is quite annoying to go through the process each time. I asked them about hypothetical scenarios such as what if I am taking a shower and don't hear the door, and what if they walk in on me and their response was "we are very professional, we will sense it if you are in the shower and won't enter". I said what if I am in my room listening music or sleeping half dressed and I don't hear the door and you can walk in on me, and they said "oh we are very professional, we will sense it". What does this even mean??? You will sense, what??

Hope they have changed their policies and they send 24 hours notices before they attempt to enter the apartment. Make sure to discuss this with them before signing the lease.

Lived at 903 S 1st for three years. Kurt and all the office staff were absolutely amazing. Any maintenance requests were responded to very quickly. Things wear and tear, and our microwave was coming to its end. We put in a request to have it looked at and got a new microwave the next day. Rent is very reasonable, and it included multiple utilities as well.  I've heard tons of complaints from my friends who rented from other companies about mold, bug infestations, water leaking from above apartments, and horrible customer service. I only moved out because I got a job out of state, but I would recommend Roland Realty to everyone.

This is the second apartment I've help my son move into through Roland Realty and I have to say they have been so wonderful to us.  I've talked to several different people and each experience has been very positive because the staff here is very responsive and wants to help as best they can.  I would highly recommend a rental unit through Roland and am thankful my son has a great apartment with them!  Thank you for all that you do!

review_text:
I lived in 909 S First (studio) for one year. It was more spacious of a studio compared to the other ones I toured. Kitchen was kinda separate from the living room/bed so i dont smell food when I go to bed. The rent is reasonable as a studio with great location on first st. But in summer the utility bill was high for me when I always had the ac on otherwise I die sweating. Btw the ac is new and really effective. heaters are too effective sometimes I feel like sitting right next to fireplace haha.

The unit I lived in was close to first st so can be noisy Thurs to Sat but no big deal. It can be noisy everywhere living on campus. I always feel grateful for them taking care of packages and other stuff. Really friendly and approachable staff to international student like me. Pool in the summer and two puppies welcoming you in the office are bonus points.

Maintenance team were very responsive too. Most of them time I submitted the service request at night and they would come knock on the door in the morning. The room was a lil bit damp sometimes so I saw bugs (not cockroaches not bed bugs). So keep the door and windows closed most of the times.

Move out process was smooth no hassle. They listened and then gave feedbacks on how to do the stuff. but I would not recommend hiring professional cleaning cuz the carpet cleaning fees are gonna be charged anyways. Do yourself a favor just try to clean up everything. I got my security deposit faster than I thought.

Overall fantastic experience living in a spacious studio by myself :))

I just rented a house from Roland Property, Kurt was very helpful and kind. He is far better anyone I talked during this house hunting period. review_text:
Money hungry leasing company who does little to maintain their buildings, yet expects their tenants to uphold perfect living standards. They are not flexible or forgiving in any aspect, and when we moved into our unit many things were out of order including dirty washers and driers, moldy showers, and other problems amongst these.

Absolutely do not lease through this company!

I am seriously so sad to be moving out of my Roland apartment. It was an incredibly spacious apartment for just two people at a very reasonable price. I lived at 903 S First, and although it is a little bit off campus, there is a bus stop for the 22 right on the street corner so I didn't have to walk anywhere far in the winter. The staff are incredibly responsive and attentive, and as accomodating as possible. With all the horror stories I hear about properties in Champaign-Urbana, I'm happy that my first apartment experience was with a trustworthy and helpful business that puts the needs of their residents first.

Renting with Roland has been great for me for the last two years. Special kudos to their leasing manager, Kurt Bulicek, who has always been of fantastic help, going above and beyond not only to present the property and answer my questions before signing the contract while I was afar, but also during the renewal process, to maintain the place when necessary, etc... as the maintenance manager can't take charge of solving any issue.

... In addition, the checkout process was sour... The company avoided to complete it with me present. They played interested in using some of my furniture, coming to see it several times, picking up some of it, and telling me several times that someone wants it. As a result, I didn't move it, only to find out the night before I was moving out that no one is picking it up anymore, so I am on my own. The next morning I left very early for a 600-mile drive, so I didn't have time to remove the furniture they said, so many time, they were interested. As a result, they charged me to remove that furniture!

Lastly, wear-and-tear does not exist with this company.
Yes, I truly enjoyed the location, but there was no investment in keeping the building clean and at least somehow current... Being stuck in the '50s.

Yet, I only received back only 56% of my security deposit, and with no interest for using those money for 2 years!!

This is a complete rip-off.

Champaign/Illinois tenant organization take note!

I had the absolute best possible experience with this company during my 4-year tenancy. Any maintenance request is addressed within a day, buildings are maintained very well, and everyone is very responsive and always willing to help. Dustin and Kurt in particular went out of their way to accommodate me whenever I needed. Thank you for everything; you will be missed.

Don't live here. When you call maintenance, they show up but don't do nothing (even something serious such as mold). One of the manager is so rude. And also, Roland likes to blame everything on their residents because they are so lazy and don't do their jobs. Seriously, don't even sign here. You'll never get anything fixed (they never fixed anything during my lease) and they'll say everything is your fault and can't do anything about it when in fact they can.

Nothing but good things to say about these guys. Our apartment had an appliance malfunction the first week, but the maintenance team had it fixed within 24 hours of when I contacted Roland. Everyone is super friendly and easy to talk to.

I'm currently subleasing and the apartment I am is absolutely disgusting. There is mold in the shower and on the walls and the apartment is moist all the time. I try to look at the better side of things but there is none here. The building adjacent is owned by Roland and is very new, nice and well kept which why it blows my mind that this one is in such bad shape. How can a company continue to build when they do not take care of the properties they already have?
I went to the office and tried to get a room condition report and was denied one though the manager was very familiar with the property and said "this is not the first complaint we have had about this property" yet they refuse to fix the issues. I will not be renting any other apts from Roland. I can't wait to get out of here.

review_text:
Was a great experience until I received my deposit back. Got charged for basic cleaning (window, baseboards, and blinds) and then basic painting. Let's not forget to mention I was the one who wiped down all of the doors and wiped the baseboards in the bedroom and closet and I made sure to take pictures and videos of all the cleaning I did. In addition to that, there was wall space in the hallway that wasn't completely painted and when I brought that to the attention of maintenance, they told me Ramshaw outsources their painters so they wouldn't have the same paint back at the office. I reached out to the office because if you have concerns about the deposit, you have to contact the office. I was in correspondence with Meredith and she was supposed to be looking into my concerns and I have yet to hear back from her. Such poor professionalism and to hold the tenant responsible for these things when you're required to take care of the space after a tenant moves out is pure theft. I can understand if a unit is just filthy beyond comprehension but I do not feel is it deserved for those of us who are clean and take the responsibility of cleaning up to the best of our ability before we move out. If I'm able to take some type of action against this I will definitely do so because I shouldn't be punished for their lack of care for their units.

review_text:
I was recently sent a survey request to my personal email Ramshaw Real Estate has record of after a completion of a work order, instead of responding to email, I thought I would leave all my surveys responses on their review pages.

To begin, I should give a quick back story. I have been a tenant in my current unit for (3) years.  I took possession of unit as a sublet and tenant prior was in unit for (2) years.  It wasn’t until I was at home more due to COVID that I started noticing a lot of issues that needed immediate and not so immediate attention.  At the time I placed a work order per my lease agreement for items to be looked at and remedied.

Per lease agreement,
My responsibility:
“Lessee agrees to call Lessor for the purpose of reporting repair or maintenance problems.”

Ramshaw Real Estate’s responsibility:
“Lessor agrees to maintain the premises in accordance with all applicable building and maintenance codes and further agrees to perform promptly all needed repairs to the premises, appliances, and furnishings, at Lessor’s sole expense, except for damage resulting from Lessee’s negligence.”

1.) How satisfied are you with the overall experience?
1 = Not at all satisfied;
5 = Very satisfied

Answer: 1 = Not at all satisfied

2.) Has the issue been resolved completely?

Answer: No

3.) Was the work completed in a timely manner?

Answer: No

Any additional feedback?  Yes, see below.

After submitting work order my Property Manager, Stephanie Maier, returned an email stating that a number of items on my work order were going to be billable.  When I responded to confirm which ones, Stephanie literally cut the whole work order and pasted it in email.  I cut what Stephanie Maier sent me and placed below for an idea of concerns.

1.) Request change of deadbolt re-cored
2.) Secure door handle
3.) Kitchen drawer repaired
4.) Fridge constantly produces water
5.) Dryer takes 12 hours to dry
6.) Washer has jeans stuck under adjatator
7.) Patio stoop deteriorating
8.) Bay window deteriorating (exterior)
9.) Closet door aligned
10.) Glass in window has a crack
11.) Screen for sliding door does not fit in door.

I completely understood that a number of items would be considered obviously billable.  I’m not that vapid.

However, what was troubling about her response was the fact that items 5, 6, 7 and 8 were all billable to me.  7 & 8 of which were due to the elements out of my control and not directly affected by my utilization of actual unit but did directly affect my bedroom wall of which held moisture.  Also, 5 & 6 were due to standard wear and tear.  Typical of machines not properly maintained.

After going back and forth with Stephanie Maier consisting of (1) email a day, communication ceased on the 10th of the month and later continued on the 14th.   The last thing Stephanie Maier stated to me in my email was,

“I cannot give specific details at this time, because no one has been there to assess the damages, other than seeing the pictures attached to the work order. Please just consider this a courtesy as charges will be assets upon completion.”

From there I waited and waited.  Occasionally checking my AppFolio portal where I submitted request and monitoring the technicians going in and out of my neighbors units.

9/24 - 12/04 - I was able to count 11 visits from technicians.

So while I patiently waited for my work orders to be looked at, I’ve seen a constant rotation of technicians onsite and in some cases handling the same issues I reported.

Then, to my dismay, my work order was cancelled months after the fact and then oddly back dated to a couple of days after it was initially put in.  After or before, not one person tried to communicate with me regarding my work orders and/or tell me the work order was being cancelled, etc.

When I reached out to Stephanie Maier regarding the cancellation this was the explanation.

“The other requests were canceled because there was a possibility
of a tenant charge on most items listed.”

I've only been leasing a few months, but whenever I submit a maintenance request they are quick and efficient at fixing. They were also accommodating when family came to visit and I needed a short term parking space even though that was technically against their current policy. The portal for making payments etc. is clear and easy to use. The apartment is not perfect (small kitchen, no central cooling...) but considering the price, it's as good as you can hope for.

EDIT

Expect them to take off half your security deposit for things like "repainting the walls".

On move out day we couldn't get in to our next lease until later in the day but they absolutely would not let us stay at the apartment for a FEW MORE HOURS. Instead we took all our stuff out on the lawn in front of the apartment and sat there waiting. nobody entered the apartment during that time so being considerate would have cost them nothing.
owner_response_text: Thank you, Oscar!

review_text: Ramshaw seems to be one of the best companies you can rent from on the UIUC campus. review_text:
We rented from Ramshae at the Tuscany Gordon facility for 3 years. Everything was decent until I started to interact with management. I'm giving two stars only because their maintenance is pretty great. Punctual, polite, and got the job done. Management on the other hand are inconsiderate and rude. About 5 months before our lease was up we purchased a home. I talked to many different people about ending the lease early. They stick to their policies (so props for that). You either pay or sublease. No exceptions - so be aware of that. I've never had a problem from other companies ending a lease early for job relocation and such. There just wasn't any understanding or negotiating despite renting from them for a couple of years. Really makes it difficult when trying to purchase a home to time it to where you don't have double payments.

The major issue I had with them is how they lied to me about our security deposit. Which I didn't receive until after our lease ended and only got it because I showed up to the office after calling twice. Here's the scenario: On 9/11 I called about where our deposit was. The lady explained that it had been sent out 8/28 according to the records. She also said just give it another week (we only live 20 miles away from the office), "don't panic". So I waited. On 10/2  I went to the office because we never received our deposit. I explained the situation to three different people. They printed a check and handed it to me. The date printed on the check was 9/12. They at least printed the check after I called on 9/11 yet they never sent it out. Not sure if others have had issues with getting deposits but it shouldn't be that sketchy to get our money - especially when they so quickly place a late fee when they want their money. Don't rent from this company.

review_text: Nice apartments for an affordable price. However, its unfortunately been the worst rental experiences I've had (have been with various companies as I've moved around for schooling and residency over the past 13 years). They allow subleasing, but have had much difficulty finding sublesees and the company was not helpful finding anyone and made no effort to re-lease the apartment. For example, I already reported twice about the peeping smoke detector in my bedroom. It appears on the system that the maintenance requests are received. But no one shew up though I asked them to fix it right away because the sound triggered my migraine. Not to mention that they moved our parking spaces to another block away without letting us knew in advance..

So far management has been more than pleasant. Unlike previous companies I have rented from they respond quickly to inquiries and problems. Their office staff is very knowledgeable about company policies and requirements. I also enjoy the fact that I am left alone as a tenant, they don’t show up like clockwork for “inspections” like some companies.
