review_text: Most people agree that JSM is probably the best landlord on the UIUC campus. Their buildings are not the newest but also not run down. However, they have tons of buildings and their own maintenance crew, so most things usually get fixed within a day or two of submitting a maintenance request. A lot of other smaller landlords take weeks or months to fix stuff, if at all, because they have to contract out the work. Their customer support at their office is very professional. However, they are by-the-books; don't expect them to bend the rules for you like a small mom-and-pop run company. The locations of the JSM properties are also quite optimal: very close to bus lines and to campus. I'm living with JSM for my 5th year now, and it's been great.

Finding my future house that I wanted to rent with some of my friends was extremely easy. They drove us to the location, informed us of everything that's included, and promptly sent another email answering extra questions that we thought of later. They were extremely flexible with the signing process, as one of my roommates is studying abroad. I would definitely suggest it to anyone that's looking to lease an apartment or house!

Best landlord in campustown. Hands-down.
Pros
1. Maintenance - 5/5 : Ive had my problems fixed in as little as 8-10 hours after putting the request online. I put a request at around 11.30pm and the guy came to fix at 8.30am.
2. Staff - very friendly. I was having a little trouble subleasing my place, and Sam was super helpful, patient, and cooperative during the process.
3. Leasing process was very easy. My rent was very very cheap! I feel we got very lucky - paying only 280/month for top notch service, and renovated apartment.
I have now moved to a new city, and I feel that JSM has spoiled me with good service. I'm hoping my new landlord is able to live up to it.

Cons

1. If you don't renew your lease, they will be showing your apartment to future tenants, but do not provide a 24 hour notice. According to Champaign laws, landlords are not required to provide any notice before showing your apartment to future tenants. This was the one thing I wish JSM did differently, but again, this is more of a problem with Champaign (Urbana on the other hand mandates notice), so I wouldn't completely blame them. I personally never felt unsafe with them entering my apartment, even in my absence, but I guess that can be a problem for some people.
2. Rent is a little higher when compared to other rentals like CPM, PPM, University group. But the quality and service is far more superior; depends on how much that matters to you.

Would definitely recommend JSM over anyone else. If you can afford it, go for it!

review_text: Viewing apartments and signing the lease were quick and easy. The apartments that I have stayed at are at excellent locations and are fairly priced. JSM is trustworthy and respond quickly to any problems or questions that I have regarding my apartment/maintenance issues.

If you go to the Tenant Union and look up the complaint records for JSM, they will tell you point blank that this management has a clause in their contract that waives your right to quiet enjoyment in your apartment: Meaning they can come in at any time & completely reconstruct your unit without your permission. Construction workers will tear your place apart from 6am in the morning to 5pm, forcing you to live somewhere else while you continue paying rent to them. They are the only property management company in the Urbana-Champaign campus area that does this.  If for whatever reason, people are still crazy enough to sign a lease with JSM, please take the time to review some of their business practices.

I lived at 406 E. Stoughton one bedroom apartment under a different realtor (a building with a long history of serious bed bug infestation). JSM bought the property while my lease with the old landlord was still active. They wanted to remodel the units into two-bed units and raise the rent for the next year, but because my lease with the old landlord prevented them from doing any superfluous construction inside our units, they used pressure tactics to force tenants to move out. (This didn't stop them from doing noisy,disruptive, construction on other units around me though). One of the managers, Emily Murphy, ignored major maintenance requests, my emails and calls for months, among many other displays of misconduct,  forcing me to contact the city inspector. The city cited 19 code violations against JSM in my unit alone. Long story short, to avoid paying fines for the code violations, JSM tried to force me out by lying that I did not comply with bed bug treatments. Then they lied that the tenant below me told them I spread bed bugs to his apartment, even though that tenant (who was actually my friend) denied this and I complied with bed bug prep instructions (with photo evidence, verified by the Tenant Union). In addition to this, the building has a LONG, recurring issue with bed bugs.Thankfully, through Student Legal Services' intervention, I received a monetary settlement and was able to move the heck out. By the time I moved out, there were only 2 tenants left out of the 12 tenants that were originally in the building.

I write this review to share my experience and also as a warning, because JSM has done this same exact thing to many of their tenants. They only care about making money and will infringe upon your rights to do so. The only good thing I can say is that maintenance staff is usually quick and friendly for *minor* issues. I encourage all prospective renters to be diligent in their research. There's no reason to sign with a company that puts language in their lease that waive your rights as a tenant.  Sign your lease with ANYONE but JSM.

-Edit-

The response from JSM is as dishonest as it is disappointing. The "renovations" were not to abate the code violations, but actually *remodel* the units - convert the one bedrooms into two bedrooms and raise the rent. (aka superfluous construction).I have advertisements for Spring 2016 from JSM's website to prove it. I also have an email from JSM regarding a major issue with my window where they admitted they weren't going to conduct needed repair at that time since they had plans to eventually remodel my unit. That same window issue was cited as a code violation months later. I also recognize some of these positive reviewers as people who work for your company & will be reporting them accordingly. I cannot stress enough  that the Tenant Union has warned  of this issue with JSM and that there are better leasing companies to choose from.

Each day has become a struggle for survival. At some point, I wake up. Immediately, I begin my day's search for WiFi connectivity. If I'm lucky, I can find a one-bar connection and attempt to send a message to my family, letting them know I am still alive, but I have been met with a, "Message could not be sent" after the WiFi quickly drops out every single time. I have survived by slowly consuming my mattress and have dug a hole in the ceiling for water with a pair of sunglasses. I spent my Christmas day determining whether or not the leftover paperclips I found in my desk on day 82 were a viable source of nutrition. Alas, they were not. I don't know how much longer I can do this. I typed this message in the event that I find a WiFi connection that lasts more than 12 seconds. If you are reading this, please help me. Please tell my family that I love them. Please tell them that I'm fighting. Please tell them that I'm alive. Please, PLEASE JSM or Pavlov Media, FIX YOUR WIFI CONNECTION.

review_text:
I am changing this review to two stars because the manager did reach out to me to address my concerns, which I do appreciate.  However, that does not make up for the lackluster experience I had while living at HERE.

It started before I moved in.  They require renter's insurance, which is not a bad thing, and through my family's insurance, this was covered.  My father and I had to supply them the document stating that I had renter's insurance at least 4 times, and again on the day that I moved in.  I am not sure if they "lost" the document that many times, but they were hard pressed to sell me renter's insurance.  This lack of accountability on their side led to a bad taste to begin.

On move in day, the person who checked me in was not friendly, and did not seem to care about their job very much.  It did not make me excited to live there.  In addition, they forgot to give me a check in document to list the status of my room and common area.  I was notified a few days later by the manager that I signed saying I had received it, but the person checking me in was rushing us so fast through the process that that fine print eluded me.  Fortunately there was no major damage in my apartment to begin, so this ended up not being a huge issue.

A few weeks after moving in, I decided to check out the "great" amenities, only to find, to my great disappointment, that most of them were either closed or in disrepair.  The movie room would not connect to a computer and the golf simulator was completely broken.  Definitely a great way to start off my stay.  The hot tub was also broken for most of the year.

Now let me get to the rooms.  When you first go on a tour, the idea of a loft suite sounds great.  It looks cool, is spacious, and overall seems like a nice place to live.  Although the rooms seem small on the tour, they feel even smaller in person.  There is no closet, except for two very large external dressers that take up half of the room.  In addition, they are in just slightly wrong proportions so nothing quite fits in the room in a way that makes sense.  As for the common room, only the bottom set of windows has blinds.  DO NOT get a room facing south (toward Green St.) as you will need to use your AC religiously.  Since the top windows do not have blinds, the sun is constantly shining in and radiating heat, making the common room of the apartment a sweat box.  So you turn on the AC.  The AC only has two settings: off or 110% on.  So if you are watching TV you are getting both boiled by sun and frozen by the AC, a pretty awful combo.  In the personal room, there is essentially no way to orient your bed so that you are not constantly being hit in the face with AC, so for anyone who wears contacts to bed, good luck.  Also, even when the weather outside is nice, the windows don't open enough to allow hardly any air in, so you are still reliant on the AC.  Which brings me to my next point...

The utilities. Now they do give you $40/person towards utilities, which is a fair amount that, assuming you are conscientious of your use, should never go over.  I ended up going over the past couple months because my roommates used the AC too much and had other uses that accounted for much of the use.  If you go over the $160 limit, they charge a $5 per person service charge, a scam plain and simple.  Now this speaks badly on Conservice, the third party utility provider for the apartment, but it also does not leave a good mark on HERE.  Unfortunately, it was in the lease that you pay a $5 service fee, so I could not get in on the class action lawsuit filed against Conservice, but in case you are interested, they have multiple class action lawsuits against them and have 1 star on Yelp.  Great company.

Speaking of the lease, this lease has the strictest guidelines on subleasing I have seen at school.  There is a $300+ fee to release, with no option to (legally) sublease.

I ran out of characters for this review, but parking is also atrocious and they said they would be breaking parking leases and they didn't, the final annoyance.

Smile(formerly Fairlawn) seems to be one of the better places to rent from on campus and I enjoyed my year with them. The apartments on Clark all are quite nice; the leasing agents and showing staff are super friendly and will be honest with you when needed. I did not find there to be any mold, rodent, or bug problems where I stayed, which you cannot say in a lot of places at UIUC.

The only things I did not enjoy was generally a lack of communication - when I submitted maintenance requests they would generally just randomly come in while I was gone a few weeks after I submitted it, do the repair, and not tell me or respond to the request; so it was always a surprise. I also rented a parking spot and 5 or 6 times in the year I would come home to one of their vehicles parked in it, and while they were friendly and quick in fixing it or giving me an alternate spot for the day, it became frustrating, especially because a few times they claimed it was not their vehicle and told me to tow only to find out it was maintenance they had hired. In the spring, they showed my apartment 10+ times in the span of two weeks and while they were apologetic about it, I believe I live in a complex full of studios so it became frustrating being basically the model apartment. Comparatively though, these issues are minor for an apartment on UIUC's campus.

I never had any major issues here, and the price I pay on the lease is very fair for a studio. If you're looking for a solid choice to rent from, this is one of two or three agencies I would actually recommend.

As a recent resident of this stunning luxury apartment complex in Champaign, Illinois, I feel compelled to share my fantastic experience with others who may be considering a move. From the breathtaking views to the top-notch amenities, every aspect of life here exudes luxury and convenience.
First and foremost, the view from my apartment is nothing short of spectacular. The floor-to-ceiling windows provide an unobstructed panorama of the city's skyline, while the natural light pouring in creates an airy and welcoming ambiance. Watching the sun rise and set each day has become a personal highlight and a constant reminder of the beauty that surrounds us.

The outdoor pool area is an oasis that instantly transports you to a high-end resort. Surrounded by comfortable lounge chairs, it's the perfect place to relax and soak up some sun after a long day. The pool itself is immaculate, with crystal-clear water that's always at the perfect temperature.

As a fitness enthusiast, I'm particularly impressed with the on-site workout room. Filled with state-of-the-art equipment and plenty of space to move, it rivals any high-end gym I've visited. From cardio machines to free weights, there's something for everyone, regardless of their fitness level. Plus, the floor-to-ceiling mirrors and ambient lighting create an inspiring atmosphere that motivates me to push harder during my workouts.

One of the standout features of this apartment complex is the attentive and professional staff. From the moment I first inquired about living here, they've gone above and beyond to ensure my every need is met. It's clear that the management team takes great pride in providing exceptional service to their residents.

The location of the luxury apartment is another major perk. Nestled in the heart of Champaign, I'm just a stone's throw away from shopping, dining, and entertainment options.

Inside my apartment, the attention to detail is evident in every corner. High-quality fixtures and finishes, such as quartz countertops and stainless steel appliances, create a modern and sophisticated living space. The open floor plan allows for seamless movement between the living and dining areas, while the spacious bedrooms offer ample storage and a restful retreat at the end of the day.

In summary, my experience living at this luxury apartment complex in Champaign has been nothing short of extraordinary. The combination of stunning views, resort-style amenities, and impeccable service has elevated my lifestyle to new heights.

It was a hectic day and I forgot to move extra money to my checking account after buying books for my classes. review_text:
The low rating is mainly due to the office staff. Unfortunately there seems to be a lot of turn over. When I moved in two years ago the girl who gave us a tour and went over our documents was very knowledgeable and able to answer any questions we had. The following are issues that I have personally had since moving in. As you can see most of them could have been avoided with good customer service.
1. Husbands credit was ran multiple times. When this was brought up to the office staff she said she didn’t know why and would have a manager look at it. We were not contacted in regards to this issue.
2. When resigning for a second year the man we dealt with seemed clueless! We went in to sign on a Saturday as that was the only day that both of us could come in together. We set up the date to come in and when we went in the guy had no clue what we were taking about. He didn’t end up getting copies of everything and we had to go back in on a different occasion.
3. No hot water for theee days. I am under the impression that staff was not aware of the issue on day 1. There was a note on the door on day 2 stating that a part needed to be replaced and hot water would be back on day 3. On day 3 there was a note saying it would be back by 5pm. Three days without hot water seemed unacceptable to me. Thankfully at the time I didn’t have a baby that needed a bottle or children who needed a bath. I spoke with management about any accommodation and was given the run around. Eventually they said that it wasn’t “major” enough like a fire to give any accommodation.
4. We have always been able to pay rent in the office....I’m unaware of any apartments where this is not a common thing. Recently we were notified that we will no longer be able to pay rent at the office. Instead we will be charged to pay rent...even though they don’t come out and say that. The new options to pay are online (with a fee-even though it doesn’t go to the apartment company it is still an additional fee that we must pay for nothing), send a check (cost of checks,stamps,envelopes and no way to verify if/when they receive rent-hello late fees and no receipt) or pay at a third party such as Walmart, Walgreens etc. which can certainly be a pain and take up time.
5. The last straw was today when I went to pick a package up from the office. I picked up one package that has been delivered the day before and asked about a second that would have been delivered today. The guy checked the packages and said it wasn’t there. I explained that I had received a notification from amazon saying it was delivered and pretty much got the cold shoulder. He didn’t check again or ask for my name/address again to make sure he was looking for the right thing. (Hello good customer service) The second I walk in my door I received a message that they had my package. I called the office and explained that I was in there within the last 2 minutes looking for the package. I also said I have a 3 week old baby and did not want to take her out in the bad weather and my husband had just left for work. I asked since it was truely their mistake if they could bring it to me (again good customer service since they were the once’s who made the mistake) he told me no and I eventually spoke with a manager. The manager reluctantly brought me my package after giving me the run around by asking if I could just pick it up the next day, explaining that all their maintenance people were gone, and that they don’t do this unless someone physically is unable to get to the office. Finally I asked if a front officer person could bring it....since there were at least 3 of them there that I know of...possibly more. Eventually my package was delivered to me.

Overall the apartments are just fine. The rooms are good size and the outside is kept up. I think the main issue is the turnover of office staff and not instilling the importance of customer service. After all, there are a lot of apartments and the only thing that can truely separate one from another is the service/s provided.

Nice place to live with some minor issues.
The good:
- Friendly, responsive staff; occasional free food in the lobby
- Full kitchen with plenty of counter space, big sink, and decent appliances.
- Everything works reasonably well
- Common spaces in the building including courtyard and lounge areas
- Gym has pretty much everything you need
- 5-10 minute walk from all the campustown restaurants
- Literally right next to Lion, if that's your thing. If it's not your thing, this is probably a negative

The meh:
- Cheap furniture; the desk chair and mattress are especially bad and I bought a foam mattress pad and proper desk chair right away. Our couch is also saggy.
- All the cabinets have terrible handles that are hard to open.
- Noisy, especially if you get a room looking out at the courtyard or Lion
- Elevators are very slow
- The wardrobe is a bit small
- It's a bit of a walk from campus, and the only really convenient bus line nearby is the green, which only stops in the middle of campus.

Overall, you can probably get better value elsewhere, but I haven't had any major issues yet, and have enjoyed the many conveniences.

review_text:
My name is Brandon Coile. Not only is their response time to service orders absolutely HORRIBLE, but after 2+ weeks of waiting for someone to come fix my dryer I bought the part and just did it myself. Their response when they got back to me and I told them thank you for nothing? They billed me $45 for “not answering service call/canceling.”. Avoid this company if you can help it.

PS: Morgan Walden is a manager at JSJ and does damage control on reviews by leaving fake 5 star reviews in response to negative reviews.

Allow me to express my sentiments regarding JSJ by commencing with the fact that they have offered residents a $50 credit in exchange for a five-star review on Google. Although my personal encounter with them warrants a three-star rating, assigning them a single star serves to restore their overall rating to a more authentic representation.

Having been a tenant with JSJ for two years, I must acknowledge that my experience has been relatively satisfactory. However, the recurring issues that persistently remain unresolved have proven to be the most exasperating aspect. In a different residence from my current one (still with JSJ), there was a persistent plumbing issue. Whenever the washer was in operation, the toilet became inoperable, and the plumbing throughout my previous dwelling was in a state of disarray, regrettably evading any resolution. Furthermore, obtaining a functional mail key took several months, and it seemed that this backlog of letters had also affected the previous tenant.

As anticipated, JSJ exhibits somewhat predatory behavior, particularly in matters pertaining to the security deposit. During my tenure last year, when the majority of the living space was covered in hardwood floors, an unwarranted charge of over $100 was imposed for carpet cleaning. Although I managed to rectify this matter, their conduct was undoubtedly unscrupulous.

The current year has presented slight improvements, albeit accompanied by certain challenges. Raccoons and squirrels have taken up residence on the roof and within the premises for as long as we have been here. The washing and drying machines have been perpetually broken, causing significant inconvenience. However, the reason prompting me to draft this review is the issue with the air conditioning. Approximately six weeks ago, the AC malfunctioned, resulting in uncomfortably high temperatures in our top-floor unit for several days. Although a claim was made that the issue had been rectified, the AC ceased to cool again after merely one week. This problem has persisted intermittently, but after submitting a fourth request and returning home to an apartment that currently registers 81 degrees, my patience is wearing thin. While I understand that unforeseen circumstances can arise, I believe it is reasonable to expect timely and effective repairs when something is malfunctioning, preferably within the first or second attempt.

In terms of landlords, JSJ falls somewhere in the middle. Their pricing is relatively fair, their responsiveness is commendable, and their staff members are pleasant to interact with. Although they do resort to unscrupulous landlord practices such as purchasing reviews and overcharging when the opportunity arises, it is essential to consider the context of residing in Campustown, where such tendencies are unfortunately not uncommon.

Renting from JSJ has been very frustrating, and I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone in the Champaign area due to the lack of timely maintenance. Generally I give workers the benefit of the doubt, especially in the climate of the job market today, but this whole experience living here as a student has been unpleasant and I cannot wait to move out and move on. I could not imagine having a family and living in these conditions either, and unfortunately would not recommend JSJ to any families to protect the health and safety of your kids just in case something goes wrong. The office staff, although friendly and cordial, are unable to give straight answers about maintenance requests and rarely actually pick up the phone. We called a total of 7 times throughout the day today without a single answer, and while they do have an answering machine available, we work 9-5 jobs and cannot pick up the phone during all hours of the day and would just end up playing phone tag. When we first moved in almost two years ago, the place was absolutely filthy as if they didn’t even inspect or clean the place before our arrival. There was a stain from what we naively presumed was an old water leak on our ceiling, which within weeks started leaking. We submitted maintenance requests and workers did come out but for an emergency that had the potential to grow mold and harm our health the response time and quality of work was not up to par. It took multiple requests for the issue to be “fixed”, but today we noticed mold growing close to the ceiling tiles (which were never replaced after the damage, they just hung up the old wet ones) that had the previous water damage before, nearly a year and a half later. We were unable to get ahold of the office today and just hope that they respond quickly to the issue as we now have two open maintance requests, including one from 11 days ago that has not been resolved.

We do have a work order open for you and are working to get the issues resolved for you as quickly as possible. We do have to address work orders in the order we receive them. review_text:
JSJ is very bad. They had termites in my apartment and blamed me for it and charging me for the damages. I'm contacting the health department. They always let their apartments slip into ruin and blame it on the tenants. So please do not lease with them.

review_text: Such quick response times and very friendly staff!! Ashley was so knowledgeable and helpful with any and all of the questions I had. I also did a showing with Jordan who was also very helpful. Great experience all the way from apartment showings to actually signing a lease.

They are nice on the phone, but once they have you on the hook to pay them money, you mean nothing to them.

My shower didn't work for two weeks once (I caved and just bought the ~$10 replacement part myself at the hardware store and installed it).

Their washers and dryers didn't work for roughly the last two months I lived there.

PLEASE READ THIS PART IF YOU FIND YOURSELF IN A LEASE WITH JSJ. I'VE SEEN ANOTHER REVIEWER DESCRIBE THIS SAME ISSUE: They are either incompetent and/or deceptive and sent my deposit to the actual apartment address (after my lease had ended...) so it was returned to them undeliverable. They did not inform me when this happened and I only finally got the deposit back after bugging them multiple times to send it.

Their favorite thing to do is blame whatever concern you have on some third party they're working with (as if somehow there is nothing they can do about it). 🙄

I recently rented an apartment from JSJ and I am very happy. I like apartment living and have had a number of landlords over the years. JSJ is certainly one of the better landlords, if not the best. When I call the office I always seem to get right through to the person who is my contact. I don't want to name names but she is always friendly, doesn't mind that I called and always seems to have (or can quickly get) the information I need  And I just had my first experience with maintenance and it was great. A very friendly (willing to listen to me) maintenance person took care of everything. He seemed to know a lot and definitely exceeded my expectations. So overall, I am quite happy I found JSJ. If you are looking for an apartment I would give JSJ a shot. And if I could, I would give JSJ more than 5 stars!

review_text: I have rented from JSJ for almost two years. Every employee that I've interacted with has been very professional. Taylor especially, was very helpful, informative, and quick to respond during my process of trying to find a new JSJ place to move into for the next academic year.

review_text: Great experience working with the leasing agent Taylor - her correspondence with me was helpful and timely. The application process was straight forward and was able to sign the lease in advance, online, which was convenient moving from out of state.

The listings were easy to browse on the website and we quickly found a unit that we were interested in that was also in our price range. Once we reached out for a tour, Morgan was incredibly helpful and available over text to answer any questions we had. It made the process much less stressful.

JSJ was a mediocre landlord for the 2 years of our lease - the property wasn’t very clean when we moved in, the house had maintenance issues that were never resolved, etc. but nothing outrageous, so whatever. Then they charged us with several dishonest security deposit fees, including about $400 for blinds that never existed in the first place. We’ve tried to contact them but they are non-responsive and refer only to an unnamed third party company handling deposits.
owner_response_text: Hi Misty. We sincerely hope we’ve resolved these issues since we’ve been in contact with you and your roommate. If you have any additional concerns, please let us know! Thank you.

review_text: I recently signed the lease through JSJ and everything was so smooth. I requested for a tour and could look around the property in a couple of days. Morgan was very friendly and responsive, and she also let me know of everything.

Expect urgent maintenance to happen between a week and a month after you start calling their office. Expect non-urgent maintenance to happen between a month and never. Every time you call them, they will claim that the person in charge of whatever you're calling about is unavailable for some reason or another, and will call you back. They will never call you back. One time both of the dryers for our building broke. A few weeks later, they replaced one with a new dryer that cost twice as many quarters. The next year, an ancient stove in the place we rented caused a gas leak. After their "repair" two weeks later, it caused another gas leak. A month after that, we finally got a functional stove. And finally, they will attempt to keep your security deposit by mailing the check to the address that you move out of, and expressing bewilderment as to why it got returned to sender. Their properties are cheap, but you get what you pay for!

This might seem like an odd review in that we didn't end up renting from JSJ. Cody worked with me to find a house. I spoke with him numerous times on the phone, and he always got back to me. He was honest in recommending properties that would or would not work for our living situation. He was polite and very trust-worthy. He truly cared about us finding the best place to live, and was not interested in getting us to sign a lease if the property didn't fit our needs. The day after we signed a lease with another company, he called to check in with me. He was genuinely thrilled that we had found a good place to live and told me he was glad for us. In our dealings with 10+ property management companies in the Champaign area, this one by far was the most professional. Thank you!

Had a leak, and Lucas the on-call maintenance not only arrived within 15 minutes of my call, he resolved the issue and even came by later to check up. Good workers are hard to find, and I was impressed his efficiency and follow up.

I have lived in an apartment for 3 years that JSJ took possession of during the summer. While their receptionists are nice, JSJ is completely unresponsive when it comes to large maintenance requests. I currently live in a house with 4 broken and rotting windows, two with broken glass. I submitted a request on 8/10/20. I haven’t had my heat work properly since I submitted a request on 9/21/20. Even after multiple calls and filing two complaints with the city, they have yet to repair either. It’s now 10/27/20.

Because of protections for landlords I still have no options in regards to withholding rent or stopping my lease. I’m basically stuck here. Do not rent from them unless you want to be on the phone up to 9 times a day (I’ve kept records of every interaction with them) asking why they haven’t sent anyone to fix the heat.

UPDATE: July 2021 and windows still not fixed fully. They have ignored maintenance requests sent in May and June. Windows have yet to be painted and one window remains sealed shut. Heat was never fully fixed, it will be a cold winter for whoever lives at W. Elm Apt. 5 next...

UPDATE: After moving out on July 31 2021, they are now trying withhold $320 of my $595 deposit citing issues that were present when I moved in. It's funny, if they claim that they properly inspected the home (remembering that I moved in 2 years before they took over the lease) then they should have seen my windows, heat, etc. and made some sort of effort to fix them, but none of that obviously happened.
owner_response_text: Hi Tanya! I apologize that this process has taken longer than anticipated with your windows. Additionally, has everything with your heat been repaired? If you are still experiencing issues please call our office and we will get someone out right away.

review_text: I have lived at a JSJ property for 3 years. In that time, any maintenance issue was handled beautifully. Very kind, very courteous.

Please do not rent from this company. They took over my apartment complex after I was living there for a year and the difference in quality of care was insane. They do not salt the parking lot nor clear off snow covered stairwells. Maintenance takes 1-2 weeks to respond if that. Broken AC? Took them a week to get someone out there to fix the water damage and a month to fix the unit. Broken gate? Takes a maintenance guy 30min to 1hour to get out there and fix it. Broken washing machine? Still waiting for them to fix it. We also had a rickety old stairwell we wanted them to fix but instead they just put yellow tape over it and we waited months for them to finally put in some better boards. Their excuse? They couldn't find a long enough ladder. review_text:
Rented from JSJ in Aug'18-July'19 at 310 Cedar St. They have bumped up renewal monthly price by $75 extra per month, so we moved.

In short - rent from JSJ only if the price and location combination is close to unbeatable. You should account for 50-100%  loss of your security deposit. Otherwise, read reviews and don't rent from JSJ.

They were supposed to return my deposit and account balance within 45 days from 07/31/19. I did not get it until days of communications (mostly one-way) and finally got it on 10/15/19, after driving to their office. Amanda (from billing?) said that she mailed the check and the breakdown of fees on August 26th. We have never received that letter and USPS delivery shows no letter from JSJ or G5 Real estate to our address. She did have the correct address.
Amanda should have emailed the breakdown of fees and she should have emailed the confirmation the same day when she mailed the checks. I hope their new manager will review JSJ's accounting internal controls.

Lastly, they took out a half of our security deposit, as everyone else mentioned. $200 for a "Touch Up walls" and $102 for carpet cleaning of a carpet that is overdue for replacement is excessive. $60 general repairs and $50 cleaning (after carpet cleaning?). We did clean up the apartment very well before move out. It was only a two-bedroom & one bath apartment.

Sloppy and terrible.

review_text: Avoid working or leasing with this company if possible. They are rude and unprofessional. Although my living experience leasing under Next Chapter Properties was pleasant, I would strongly recommend staying away from the company. Upon vacating the property at the end of the lease, they illegally charged me a considerable number of move-out fees. These include fees for paint touchups, carpet vacuuming, and general cleaning. This is illegal under Urbana city law section 12.5-20d. They also failed to provide me with the itemized, paid receipts which is illegal under Urbana city law section 12.5-20a.

After speaking with the management about the illegal and unethical charges, it’s clear that I was not the only one given these bogus charges. The property manager told me that “99% of our tenants go above normal wear and tear.” This shows a pattern of gross incompetence and negligence in their duties as a landlord. The landlord must provide a burden of proof showing verifiable damages that would otherwise interfere with use of the living space. Otherwise, these are simply fanciful claims that do not meet any sort of legal definition. I went back into the unit to inspect the work they did and it turns out they never actually painted the walls or cleaned the carpets as they claimed.

The documents they did provide me show that they hire contractors to do cleaning and painting over the entire building and then split up the charges to each room. This is yet again illegal since the charges and bills must be itemized and specific to each unit. If you lease from them, it’s likely that they will hit you with these same fraudulent charges as well.

While the buildings themselves are nice and have plenty of amenities, it wasn’t worth it in the end. If you don’t mind being charged illegally, having your entire security deposit withheld, and spending months fighting them to return the money they legally owe you, then you may enjoy living there though. Otherwise, it’s in your best interest to look somewhere else.

4/17/23: My first year at Fairlawn Village was great, no issues! However, this past year I have had a multitude of issues, most recently a problem with the kitchen plumbing that has yet to be addressed. On 2/10/22, I submitted a maintenance request that dirty water was bubbling into my kitchen sink when my neighbor ran their garbage disposal, and since then I have not been able to use my sink at all. After inspection, it was determined that there was a break in the sewer line. The reason that the sinks are not draining is because the break has allowed debris into our plumbing. I was instructed to run water into a tub and dump it outside until the break got fixed. They arranged for someone to come by in March to fix the issue, however when I asked Fairlawn about the plumbing company's procedures for containing asbestos (this building was built in a time when asbestos was used in nearly everything), they ghosted me. It's been over two months and, despite multiple requests, the issue has still not been fixed.

It's now gotten to the point where I woke up this morning to water pooled under my sink due to the leak. Very frustrated all around, this is definitely not worth the $800+ I pay in rent every month. It's clear that they want to take the cheapest way out when fixing things, to the point where they'll just ignore you if you ask for basic safety procedures to be followed. I've gotten sick multiple times after coming in contact with this contaminated water. It's absolutely ridiculous that Fairlawn allows this to happen. Save your time and live at a property that actually cares about your health and wellbeing.

Update 5/2/23: Despite their reply stating that they'd be in contact with me, I haven't received a single update from the maintenance department. Still unable to use my sink! Do NOT rent with Fairlawn if you value communication and quick, effective maintenance.

Update 7/12/23: I received my security deposit back, or at least 1/8th of it. They really had the audacity to charge me for sink cleaning even though I literally COULD NOT USE MY SINK WHEN I MOVED OUT! (For those of you counting, that is one hundred and eleven days without a working kitchen sink) In fact, it was sealed off completely because the horrible smells coming from it were making me sick. They also took $350 out of my security deposit for painting and, after requesting it over two weeks ago, have failed to produce any sort of itemized receipt explaining what painting they did. I find it hard to believe that there was $350 worth of painting that had to happen due to circumstances beyond normal wear and tear. Why the consistent radio silence????? Fairlawn continues to be a nuisance in my life- STAY AWAY.

review_text:
I had a horrible time with getting anything repaired while living at Fairlawn. Most of the issues, like a toilet that would continue to run water every few minutes, wouldn't have been a big deal; but I had a months-long horror story with a carbon monoxide leak. Which, as is fairly common knowledge, can be fatal.

The first time my carbon monoxide detector went off was in November. We called maintenance, and a guy was sent out the next day. He inspected the furnace, and discovered that one of the two pilot burners was not lighting because the air vent was rusted over. So, he cleaned it up, said that they would be along to do more work, and gave us an additional CO detector.

We never heard back from them with regards to the continuing work. And, from then until February, periodically our detectors would go off if the furnace was running. Any further maintenance calls resulted in them sending us an additional CO detector; by the end, we had 6 in a 1000-sq-ft apartment.

Then on a Saturday night in February, when we couldn't get ahold of maintenance at 4:50pm when they were supposed to be available til 5pm, we were finally forced to call out the Urbana Fire Department, who verified that their equipment also showed an elevated CO level near the furnace - over 5 times the "safe" limit. The gas company was then called out, and they told us that, for safety's sake, they had to shut off the gas. On a 40 degree night in February. We FINALLY got a call back from Fairlawn's emergency maintenance staff two and a half hours later, at which point we were sitting in the car with our dogs. The guy had the gall to ask if we still needed someone sent out. He ended up bringing us 3 space heaters for the night.

That following Monday, we went and spoke with office management in person. The lady there tried to tell us that, since Ameren had been forced to turn off the gas, this was an Ameren issue, and not one that Fairlawn should have to address. This contradicted what the Ameren technician had told us - the issue was with the furnace and internal piping, and therefore the landlord's purview - and we told her as much; but she wouldn't believe us until we sat down in the lobby and called Ameren on speakerphone.

At this point, they FINALLY agreed to send out maintenance to replace our furnace. The new furnace was installed promptly, but afterwards, there was a leak in the ceiling around the furnace vent because it hadn't been sealed properly. I also got a call a few weeks later from an external HVAC tech saying that he needed to come out and double check the install... Because Fairlawn hadn't gotten it properly permitted with the city of Urbana beforehand.

So, when our lease ended, we have since moved out of Fairlawn's property. And I would DEFINITELY not recommend them to anyone looking for a reasonable place to rent. In that three month span, the lives of myself, my partner, and my dogs were all constantly at risk due to negligence on Fairlawn's part. Go check out Royse Brinkmeyer's places instead, honestly.

I am giving this review as both a resident at Fairlawn Village and a owner who hires Fairlawn real estate to manage my property.

Fairlawn real estate who took over the business around 2015 is definitely the best one in taking care the community. They mow the grass every two weeks in the summer, shovel the snow in time in the winter, fix the external of the building as soon as there is a need, send out staff to pick up the garbage in the neighborhood regularly, and so on. They really do keep the neighborhood nice and neat. I can see staffs working on different things every day when I walk my dog in the community. Staffs are really friendly to work with, and they stop and say hi to you as you pass by!

As a owner: I am moving out of my unit this summer and I hired Fairlawn Real Estate to manage my condo (after I interviewed five other management companies). They are very professional in explaining all the details to me. They also coordinate the remodeling of the condo. The condo is rented after one tenant visit. Their management fee is reasonable, and comparable to other property managements in the area.

Overall my experience of with this company have been very positive, and I hope they can keep up the good work. I will give another review on property management after some time.

I am a current resident of The Maywood at Speedway in Indianapolis. My roommate and I moved into The Maywood in June 2020, while it was still known as Lexington Green under Barratt Asset Management. The change in management to Fairlawn marked the start of a rapid decline.

Since the new management company has taken over my experience living here has been awful. To start, contacting anyone in the office is basically impossible. I have been hung up on, left on hold for extended periods of time, or the phone has simply not been answered. There have been two separate occasions where the power in my unit has gone out while the rest of the building remained unaffected. The first time this happened I was left without heat for over 16 hours in the middle of the winter. I have not been given an explanation, nor offered an apology, for either of these incidents.

I overlooked these incidents and was considering renewing my lease until another incident occurred. I noticed I was being charged $25 for parking, despite my lease explicitly allotting two free parking spots. My roommate was able to reach someone in the office, Tiffani Brinkley, who stated that management DID NOT HAVE A COPY OF OUR LEASE, but asked us to send a copy. After reviewing it, Tiffani told us that our parking situation with the previous management would be honored and that we would be credited the $25 fee that we already paid. Under the impression that the situation was handled, my roommate and I thought nothing of it. After hearing the complaints of other tenants regarding the poor management practices, we made the decision that we would not be renewing our lease.

A month later, we noticed that we were charged another $25 parking fee. Not only that, the previous $25 credit had NOT been added to our account. My roommate then called the office (multiple times before getting an answer) and briefly spoke to Brandon Slaton, who said that he would look into it before hanging up.
Later on, I was told that the now $50 in fees wouldn’t be refunded and that I would have to park somewhere else. Nevertheless, I kicked up enough fuss to eventually have the $50 credited back.

There have been a slew of incidents of management malpractices made by Fairlawn staff. WAYYY too many to list in one review. In March, we were informed that our gas bill was going to be TRIPLED due to the snow storm in Texas. When asked for clarification and why a storm in Texas affects gas prices in Indiana, they stated that “they get gas from Texas”. This company's poor management has led to an EXODUS of tenants (most being elderly, Black and/or Hispanic) that have been living here for 10-15 years. This is being done intentionally to cater to young, white future residents.

Even today, I was issued an EVICTION NOTICE despite the fact that the rent was clearly paid on time just as it always has been. After calling the office seven times to no answer and going directly to the office to be ignored (there were obviously people inside), I finally sent an email that was responded to with a poorly written, condescending email, full of grammatical mistakes that explained that the notice was sent in error. Wouldn’t it have been simpler to just answer the phone? Why is it always an ordeal to get in contact with anyone in the office? These are just a few of the issues I’ve experienced since Fairlawn took over.

Also, the property manager, Brandon Slaton, is just awful. His condescending nature and disrespectful attitude has made it clear that he doesn't care about anything other than making money. NEVER in my years as a renter have I experienced such inept management. I am counting down the days until my lease is up and I can be free of this place. I have never had an issue with management before on any property I've lived on, I have never been late on any type of payment, nor have I ever had any other major issues before Fairlawn took over.

So, if you want to be treated like an actual human being and live in a place that has even a bare minimum standard for management, STAY AWAY FROM THE MAYWOOD AT SPEEDWAY!

Bad:

My experience at One North has been well worth it for the two years I've spent here. There are SIX factors as to why I believe One north is one of the BEST apartment areas to stay in.

1) The staff and managers who work here are all professional and know how to handle people with respect; very personable and friendly (Not rude).

2) They are quick and efficient with maintenance requests to make sure people's living areas are o.k. (Living areas if kept neat by residents are nice to live in too and I love the set up of the apartments). Also, they do frequent upgrades to certain parts of apartments to make living better. Maintenance guys are also respectful.

3) The entire One North community for the most part is a peaceful one; not too noisy. One north has strict policies to make sure this isn't an attraction of rowdy apartments. One north has security guards frequently around to check out areas. (Other apartment complexes I know of DO NOT HAVE THIS and this is very important to me)

4) There is a swimming pool, basketball court, tennis court, volley ball court, gym, and area outside where when it's nice out, a person can barbecue. Nice scenery and much to do in leisure time.

5) The fact that the workers and managers at One North actually take the time TO GET TO KNOW THE RESIDENTS is good too. By trying to reach out and be involved with the residents and actually sending out emails to residents to keep us aware of what their planning. To be honest I've never experienced this before anywhere else. Examples: Hosting movie nights for staff and residents. Ordering food from restaurants and allowing residents to come in and eat for free, etc..

6) The management here is pretty reasonable as well; willingly to work with you on late rent due to whatever financial issues and not quick to evict unless necessary.

I've lived at One North for two years and it's an excellent value with really good amenities (especially the gym), and friendly staff. Management has always been helpful and responsive to any issues; as a graduate student, it's been a quiet place to live during my time at Illinois.

The balcony space is nice and supports the coziness. Maintenance requests are responded to rapidly, and the staff is usually prompt to answer emails. They allow pets, with fees of course.

The Bad: This place needs a major remodeling. Seems like it hasnt been since the 80's. Upkeep of the grounds is sub-optimal. For God's sake, someone do some landscaping on the bushes. They are unsightly and gnats nest in them during the summer, coming out and into your place through the air conditioners (which are old and wall-mounted). The gym has been recently "upgraded." However, the treadmills are just there for show. They don't even work!!

When I moved in, I was offered a cheap mattress and box-spring by the manager  because I didn't have bed at the time. I loved in to find the set there in the bedroom with a dark stain on it and a deep deep dent in the middle! Why would he even give this to me?? It should have been in the garbage.

T&C offers rent credits for referrals. Interestingly, these referral credit offers keep increasing over time. With the state of the grounds, i'm surprised they can afford it. Don't think it'll be so simple to obtain your credit though. You better stay on it.

Overall, I didn't enjoy my stay as much as I enjoyed laying on the carpet in my apartment. If you need a low-barrier option for a place, here's a choice. If you expect more out of the management though, dont even look here. You can probably find something better around C-U for a comparable price.

Part 1. Gather Illinois presents a pretty face that hides the gross incompetence of its staff and shoddy workmanship. Having been at UIUC for over 7 years, I can confidently say this is the worst living experience I have had.

To begin, the first red flag was that I found someone pretending to sublease a unit for a discounted price on Facebook. When I asked to view the place, she said she wasn’t sure how to go about that, to contact the office. It turns out that she was the leasing manager. The discounted rate was actually in the form of an “incentive agreement” to provide a $1500.00 gift card that “could be used towards rent.” To date, I haven’t been able to confirm that, because I haven’t received it, despite the contract stating I’d receive it “within 30 days of move-in.”  It has been over 30 days. The company hasn’t responded to my emails. The manager is always busy or out of the office when I call, and his staff tells me they don’t know when he’ll be in when I ask. When I finally found him in his office. He said it is out of his hands. He tried to say I didn’t move in when I moved in, etc. Finally he promised it would be no later than “Thursday” which has now passed.  Again, he was unavailable and hasn’t responded to my email.

As for the building. I didn’t receive most of my furniture until after a month of moving in. I'm still missing things under the bed. Every time I asked, they kept telling me they emailed me about it, but I told them I hadn’t received one. Other units, still haven’t received their furniture. Again, promise after promise, one false reassurance after another.

Regarding the furniture, it is hurriedly put together by minimum wage workers on the concrete outside, often blocking the door. When not distracted by them fighting with each other or complaining to you about the manager, you can see the surface of your tables, desks, etc. being dragged around the cement. Keep in mind that these random workers that complain to you outside about how little they get paid have been randomly entering our apartments without notice and even while we’re away. I will come home one day and something will be installed. I see them walking in and out of other people’s apartments. There’s a reason they require renters’ insurance. Keep track of your belongings. This rushed and unprofessional work is also seen in your apartment.

The floors of my unit have deep scratches in them from things being dragged around during assembly. The cabinets and shelving also have scratches on them. Keep in mind this is a brand-new building. Drywall work is shoddy at best. There are corners that aren’t even squared, areas where they simply painted over the drywall tape prior to proper sanding. Also, If you care about noise, look elsewhere. Perhaps they cut costs on insulation or forgot it completely as another oversight. This is the loudest building I’ve lived in during my 7 years at university. You can hear the people above you and beside you. You’ll wake to doors slamming in the halls (the doors self-slam when they shut automatically) and you can hear even quiet footsteps and conversations happening down the busy halls.

I attempted to transfer units within 24 hours of move-in. They told me I could. That I’d hear back Thursday. I didn’t. I filed a formal request online. No response. I went in, again, and they assured me this could happen, that the other unit wasn’t finished. The next time I followed up, they pretended those conversations never happened and told me it was leased and they had no units to transfer me to. 3 weeks later, I finally received a response to my formal request, denying it.

review_text:
Parkside Apartments is a great place to live!

The rent here is fair, there’s a bus stop right next to it to help with going places, and they accommodate dog owners such as myself quite well by having a little dog park and an assortment of dog waste bag dispensers scattered across the property.

Aside from those things, the staff here are great. Mary does a great job managing things in the office and is a very friendly and professional individual. The maintenance folks are also awesome. Not only are they quick to check up on issues you bring up, one of the guys often has dog treats and really makes the day of my dogs when he surprises them with a treat.

I’ve been here since Fall 2019 to work on my PhD and I’ve seen ownership of this place change in that time. The new ownership has done a great job improving the place, adding things like the dog park and the gazebo with outdoor seating and fire pit. The new ownership even added digital means of paying rent, modernizing the place and making things much more convenient, compared to the old ownership who made you pay by check. So yeah, the increasing in ratings here are well deserved!

We’ve always liked living here due to a number of reasons, but since changing management things have gotten progressively much better (specially when thinking about the common areas of the community). Maintenance has always been AMAZING, we just couldn’t be happier with how fast and reliable they are. We love having a small dog park here and management has done a good job keeping it tidy despite some people not being that great at picking up after their dogs. Rent price is unbeatable for the area and our apartment is in great condition with “wood” flooring and nice size bathroom/bedrooms. I’d say in general, this is a quiet place to be in and the new management people are very friendly and helpful. Hopefully in the future they’ll think about adding more features such as lockers for packages, for example.

I’ve been living at my apartment for about maybe 5-6 yrs now. I love it! I feel safe, my baby dog has a place where he can be off his leash at the dog park, and it’s clean. The staffs are very friendly and wonderful! I can count on them for anything that needs to be taken care of or just a friendly smile. I would definitely recommend Parkside apartments to my friends and family.

It’s a great place to rent from. I love the maintenance crew. The only few down sides is that 1. There is no central air which makes it super hot near the back of the apartment unit during the summer. 2. I feel there could be car ports to protect vehicles when weather is inclement. I love Mary  and Jim and his crew. Sad to see prices have grown up slightly but that due to the market. Everyone seems to be kind and courteous. Everyone tend to themselves. If you’re looking for a place that’s low key and not super noisy this is your place. Again many great things to say so little time. Besides those two things I love this place makes you feel safe to with the double door lock system as well.

Moved in a couple years ago and so far it has been awesome! One of the best places to live considering it's close to the campus and the rent is a lot less than other places now. The repairs are always done same day/next day, packages can be delivered to the office or there are safe mailbox spaces that the packages can be locked in. Office management people are always easy to reach and super nice, and plans for monthly events. The overall apartment is kept clean and tidy and the only complaint I have is that the lock on my door is a bit janky, but that's it! (I have the unfurnished unit with carpet floor and not upgraded kitchen).

This place is also pet friendly :) Extremely reasonable pet charges compared to other places.

I am a current tanent here and this place has been great. The maintenance guys are wonderful to work with and people in the neighborhood are friendly and nice. The apartments are next to some great running routes that I use and have been very safe both during the day and night. I would highly recommend living here considering all the amenities, people, services, and the surrounding areas. Extra points for the wonderful people in the office.

review_text: I have lived here for two and a half years now and have really enjoyed it. The rent is very reasonable and the management is very responsive. They give you plenty of freedom with what you can do with your apartment, and are always very kind. The only downsides are that deliveries are often left outside for others to see, or in the rain. Also the outside locks on the buildings aren't very secure. Your own apartment has a very secure deadlock, so no real complaints there. The laundry is mediocre, but it is right outside my apartment, so again, not a big deal. Even being an apartment, it has a decent dishwasher and a full size water heater. I expect to live here for as long as I rent in Champaign-Urbana.

I lived at Parkside for two years while attending UIUC. It's very close to campus and there's also a bus stop right outside the gate (although I never rode from that stop so I can't talk about it). The types of people living here are a few undergrads, lots of graduate students, and then families/couples. There's a Meijer in your backyard as well and my favorite Mexican spot in Chambana, Huaraches.

Some issues: Since we lived on the top level we ended up with a leak in our bathroom during fall '18. It took about two months to fix and I think it was mainly due to the maintenance guys not being the most efficient or responsive people. It was uncomfortable to deal with during that time but eventually it was taken care of. The great thing is we were compensated for the trouble and management offered alternatives so we didn't have to use our bathroom. Also, there's new maintenance who are great at what they do. They replaced our pantry light and fixed our fan within an afternoon.
Every now and then we would get visits from local scams (the usual energy supplier alternatives). After it happened enough, locks were installed on the doors to the buildings. A little tricky if you have tons of groceries, but way worth it to not have to deal with those people.

Positives: During the winter I felt no danger leaving my car running in the morning. Management is quick to respond and very accommodating. Parking wasn't an issue, people basically take the same spots every time. Seems very pet friendly. Not far from anything.

Overall, I would recommend Parkside to anyone wanting to live in the Champaign-Urbana area. If you're a student who wants to live off-campus this is a great option, I never felt out of the loop since it's just a quick drive to campus. Oh, we also got our deposit back so that's always a plus.

Pros:
-Wonderful maintenance staff that are very prompt and friendly!  5+ Stars
-Clean and well kept property outside.
-Clean, recently remodeled well maintained apartments inside.
-Very efficient with utility costs, especially being on a middle floor.  I like the fact one can control the heat in each room.  Saves money.
-The sink dish sprayer things actually work!!  At least in my apartment.  I've never seen one of those work properly before in my entire life..LOL
-Rental costs are very reasonable considering how nice the place is.  It's not like the other numerous rat holes in Urbana.

Cons:
-No objective proof but I highly suspect some mold growth behind the walls in SOME of the lower unit apartments, in the hallway areas it seems.  At least in my unit.  If you move in here make sure to get a middle or upper floor apartment.  The basement one's are musty and mildew may collect on your clothes and things like that.  I moved up-stairs halfway through my stay at Parkside and it was much better and with bigger windows too.  The air circulation in general is not very good here.  Due to windows being all on on one side there is no cross breeze.  A fan in the window can help.  The laundry rooms and hallways get a bit humid, dirty, and stinky sometimes due to poor air circulation.
-There are too many DOORS with turning knobs to go through to get to one's apartment.  Bringing groceries home in this regard can be a bit of a pain in the butt.  All those doors also cut down on the air circulation even more making the hallways a bit smelly at times.
-Moving out I cleaned up extremely well but they were still very nit picky about every little thing that I felt should have been considered "normal wear and tear", they took half my deposit away which I was not real happy about.  A couple issues they had were valid but I wish they would have let me know what to look for and I would have taken care of them before I left so I wouldn't be charged.  Like dusting the ceiling fan for example I was charged $10 for.  I mean seriously!  I could have done that myself easily  but it's just not something you think of.  They charged me $80 for carpet cleaning.  I left it well vacuumed and near spotless.  Well of course the carpet is going to need a deep clean after having lived in that unit nearly 4 years.  They do this service each time anyway before someone new moves in.  If you move here don't expect all of your deposit back no matter how clean and nice you make it.  I now regret spending multiple hours cleaning and making sure the place was near pristine before I moved out.  Why bother with some of it when they're going to charge you for stuff anyway.
- I kind of felt like just a number living here sometimes especially after the original tenant Jackie left.  The place just felt colder...like they could care less if you stay or go so long as they get their money on time.
-Most of the neighbors don't know each other or rarely if ever even go outside.  I'd often go outside but almost never ran into anyone.  A few people maybe, but for the most part everyone pretty much just kept to themselves.
-Not necessarily a good place if you have kids or like to play your stereo system every once in a while in the middle of the afternoon.  If you like dead quiet however (Which I personally don't), then it's a pretty decent place to live.  Some tenants seemed very picky about sound.  Complaining about me playing my electric piano at normal levels and things like that in the middle of the afternoon.  I could see at night time  but not mid-day.  Just silly.

Overall my experience was a good one at Park-side which is why I continued to stay there for as long as I did.  I only moved out when the opportunity to get a house came along.  Otherwise I'd still be there.  Quite happy overall.   I would recommend this place for those looking to save money.  The apartments are very nice, clean, and spacious.  For the price it's a great deal.  Any issues that you have they are very prompt and friendly to work with you.

We lived here for about 1 and a half years and overall had a good experience.

The apartments are clean and well maintained. The units are laid out so that you have one neighbor across the hall and one neighbor that shares a wall with you. We had noisy, rude neighbors on the shared wall for a few months. We complained to management and they took appropriate action by sending them warnings. The noisy neighbors were gone within a couple months.

Management and maintenance were always friendly and easy to work with. They responded promptly to any issues we had. For example, our window AC unit went out in the middle of the summer and they replaced it with a brand new one the same day. On another occasion, our keys suddenly stopped working (the lock was worn out, not even their master key would work on it). We called the emergency maintenance number and they arrived within a half hour and replaced the lock.

Air flow in the interior walkways is very minimal. It tends to smell in between apartment units when tenants cook food or don't clean up after their animals.

The laundry room is on the bottom floor in between apartment units. It tends to get very warm and steamy when tenants do many loads of laundry in a short amount of time. It has caused the fire alarm to go off once or twice. They turned off once the room was aired out a little bit (there was no actual fire).

We did extensive apartment hunting before choosing Parkside. We thought the rent was affordable. It is much less expensive and you get more for your money compared to what you will get on campus.

We think it's a good neighborhood and have not had any crime issues. There are a few security cameras looking over the parking lot.

They also have a sister complex down the street called Stoneridge. We also liked those, but decided on Parkside because it was a little less expensive and closer to the bus route.

Parkside is right on the 5 Green MTD bus. It is convenient for UIUC students going to campus (about 15 minutes to the Illini Union, which is not too bad for being off campus).

Parkside tenants are students, families, couples, and bachelors. We have not had any issues with loud parties or excessive music. There is always enough parking for ourselves and guests. Parking is free for tenants and guests, too!

Regarding our deposit, we got almost all of it back besides the carpet cleaning fee.

We are only moving because of a job relocation. We were happy with our time here at Parkside and would recommend to others looking for a place to live!

Where do I even begin? My friends and I started the apartment search pretty late in the game and were concerned that we wouldn't be able to find an apartment that we loved. However, what I appreciated about CC is that management here is super friendly, helpful, and accommodating in getting us housed for next year.

Of course, CC isn't the only apartment with competitive features. However, here are some features that really won our hearts:

- Fantastic Amenities: 20 study rooms with screens and open tables? This is a student's dream, and as a telecommuter, I'm even more impressed with how every floor has a handful of conference rooms for group or individual studying. The clubhouse, gym, etc. are really nice, but the sheer number of conference rooms far exceeded any that we saw in other apartment complexes.

- Location, Location, Location: Proximity to the Engineering library on campus is key. You can bike, bus, or walk to campus in a matter of minutes.

- Super responsive management: Shout out to ZACH! Every email, phone call, question, etc. was fielded promptly and with a friendly willingness to help. Zach even stayed after hours to help clear up any of myriad of questions and get through the application/lease signing process. I saw other residents pop in and out of the leasing office for random requests, and there were always a handful of staff that jumped on to help them.

- Diversity & Community: It's no big secret that UIUC hosts a rich demographic of students from various backgrounds. It feels friendly, community-like, and safe and I see really cute decorations hung up around people's doors celebrating their cultural background. Every resident I've run into has been nice, and I see various people walking their dogs around. It feels like a nice dorm experience but with an upscale swing.

- Parking: CC has way more affordable parking than other vendors out there. And during the winter when it snows, you'll want covered parking if you own a car.

- Layouts: The units that we visited (and I visited friends' non-model units as well for a "real look") were pretty clean and comparable to the ones we saw online through pictures. I like the kitchen island space since I do plan on cooking a lot, but the furnishings are convenient if you don't want to move in/out a lot of items.

I can't speak much for the roommate selection process since I'm moving in with friends I already know, but each one of the rooms can lock according to a keyfob so it seems to be reasonably safe & private if that's your thing.

Needless to say, my friends and I are super stoked to be able to move in :) Good luck on your apartment search, everyone!

review_text:
The parking garage gates broke 5 times in the first month I lived here before they stopped getting repaired. Management blamed it on a delivery driver, but that doesn't excuse it happening so many times and it doesn't excuse poorly designed gates (you can easily drive in after a resident who has a gate tag, and then be trapped in the garage with no way to open the gate and no clear signage for delivery drivers that the gates operate by tag only). Management has "contacted their vendor," but that was months ago and there's been no update.

The key fob entry for the exterior building doors doesn't work anymore, leaving most exterior doors fully unlocked. Happened around the same time as the garage gates, and management gave the same answer. "We've contacted out vendor." Either their vendor is incredibly slow or they never did contact them, because the doors still don't work.

The key fob entry for my unit stopped working, meaning I couldn't lock the door from the outside. And for some reason the doors don't have physical keys for redundancy. It took several maintenance requests, emails, and calls for us to finally get it fixed so we could lock our door when we go to class. Campus Circle may claim that holiday hours were to blame for the delay, but on the day they were supposed to be fully open we still could barely get a hold of the office. And also, shouldn't they have some manager on hand for emergencies like this? Especially considering that the exterior doors STILL don't lock anyone off the street could have walked into my apartment when I was gone.

Not to mention the other issues mentioned in these reviews. The pool hasn't been open since I got here. The package pickup is slow at best so I just order my packages to amazon lockers. There's been a spilled pint of ice cream hidden behind a hallway door since October that custodial staff hasn't cleaned. They advertise internet and cable, but the internet is a single public network (so I just set up my own router anyway) and the cable signal looks absolutely garbage. The parking garage is so narrow and has blind turns, which is made worse by a lack of mirrors and center lines, resulting in near head on collisions every week.

They'll certainly have excuses related to their vendors, other residents, and delivery drivers. But the fact of the matter is that the building and its facilities are poorly thought out and poorly maintained. If it weren't for the rent concession I got for signing early this year, I could easily get better for cheaper.

At least the front desk staff are all nice.

review_text:
UPDATE:

Some leasing team members later took the responsibility and helped me solve the issue. Special thanks to the diligent and exceptional work of Whitney, who really cares how residents feel.

-----------------------------------------

When I was in the process of selecting a unit, I was recommended for my current one with what was described as "premium features", notably including big windows. I was also shown a model room (regular one) in which the window was openable, which is important to me as I care about air freshness and humidity.

However, upon moving into the actual unit, I discovered that all the big windows in my unit are not openable, thereby depriving me of any natural air flow. This detail was never communicated to me by the leasing team beforehand, and the misrepresentation in the model room further misled me in my decision-making process. If I had been made aware of this, I would have certainly opted for a different unit.

Moreover, I find it objectionable that I am charged an additional fee for this the big window as "premium feature" – about an extra $15 per month. What adds to my concern is this big window seems to be simply a combination of two standard windows, which can be found in many other regular units (so not necessarily "big").

While I would like to believe that this omission of information was not intentional, unfortunately, it does give the impression of dishonesty. More sadly, when I approached one of the managers seeking a resolution or potential compensation for this issue, I felt a bit brushed off without a real discussion or any meaningful effort to address the situation by just stating that's what the rule is.

I'd really appreciate if we could revisit this issue and find a fair resolution. It is important to ensure residents feel heard and valued that any information provided can be trusted and any concerns are addressed promptly and fairly.
owner_response_text:
We appreciate your detailed feedback and apologize for the inconvenience you've faced regarding the windows in your unit. We understand your frustration and acknowledge that our communication could have been clearer in this regard.

While it's not typical for us to explicitly mention that windows are non-openable during tours for a select amount of premium units with big window views, we recognize that this detail is important to you, and we're sorry for any misalignment between your expectations and the actual unit. We genuinely strive to provide accurate information during the selection process.

We did our best to fulfill your preferences based on your description, and we understand that we fell short in meeting your expectations in this specific aspect. Your feedback highlights an area where we can improve to ensure our residents' needs and preferences are better understood and addressed.

Thank you for giving us the opportunity to address this matter. Your input is valuable, and we're committed to learning from this experience and enhancing our communication and service going forward. If there's anything else you'd like to discuss or if you have further questions, please feel free to reach out to us directly.

review_text: I have lived in many apartments. This apartment is my favorite. I didn’t have any issue with management. Managers were considerable and caring.
