*Updated for 2023*
My husband and I lived at Element from 2020-2022, and only relocated due to my husband's work. I can still honestly say that it is the best rental experience we have ever had, bar none. I highly recommend for anyone looking!

Marty is extremely attentive to the maintenance issues of the building. It is very well kept, and he does such a good job on everything. He is observant, proactive, and very respectful of tenants. Whenever we have had to put a maintenance request in, the issue is resolved within an extremely reasonable amount of time (has always been next day in our experience), and he even takes the extra moment to tell us what the issue is, how he has fixed it, etc. It is always a pleasure to run into him within the building or on the property.

Toni is downright amazing in her role, we lucked out. Whenever we have had issues, she is on top of it without hesitation. I cannot say enough wonderful things about her. She is extremely knowledgeable, considerate, and really is concerned about the status of the building, the tenants, and any/everything that goes on here. She is very patient, and accommodating, and for that, we are truly grateful.

Don't skip touring this building. We almost did because the pictures don't do the units justice. It's a great value for the money in comparison with other complexes in the area, and you can really get a lot of bang for your buck. I feel like there is something for every budget here. There are a mix of unit types, from studio apartments to three bedroom units. My husband and I toured several, all were very nice. Some are more updated than others, thus there are different price points and such. We have always felt safe and secure here, the building does appear dated- but it's very well kept and looks can be deceiving. When we moved in, the apartment was clean overall- I did do some detailing, but nothing I wouldn't have done elsewhere.

Pros: Secure building, pet friendly with reasonable rates, on site amenities, manager on site, maintenance on site, consistent pest control, laundry on site (we were initially off-put by this, as we were used to having in unit, but don't let that scare you. It's not much of a dent in the budget), cost efficient, walkable to major grocery stores and DT Urbana events/restaurants, neighborhood feels safe and is beautiful/historic, discounts just for being a resident at local businesses, they have partnered with rentplus- which will report your on time rent payments to credit bureaus and help with your credit score if needed, secure parking available depending on budget, plenty of free street parking and a guest parking lot, a lot of diversity.

The little nuances that might be a con to some people: it takes some getting used to the temperature differences that can be experienced in the hallways-  they can be very humid in the summer time if you're sensitive to that and it doesn't affect units and won't have to spend much time in them. They are heated in the winter when it counts.
The AC unit can be a little loud and takes some getting used to. I was initially concerned about having a wall unit but it has actually saved us money in the long run.
Neighbors can be disrespectful- the things we have noticed most- not picking up after their dogs, littering around the building, smoking in units and common areas, noise/smells, lacking care for the building and facilities, letting delivery drivers in and giving friends the secure codes, leaving outside doors open. This is in no way management's fault of course, and is subject to apartment living. Toni stays on top of this stuff and there are consequences for them, which is reasonable and good.

My unit is unfurnished, which lowers the rent and is nice, but most of them already have furniture. The sunlight on the south building is outstanding - helps keep it warm in the winter. The theater and rec rooms at the front are nice if you want to have friends over for events. I lived in ONE South for a semester - Capstone is much, much better. TL;DR

I lived in Capstone for 2 years. When I received my post move-out charge sheet last week, I got a 85 bucks penalty for breaking their mattress spring box. THE SPRING BOX WAS ALREADY BROKEN at the time when I moved in. The reason why I didn't note it in the move in inspection is that unlike other furnitures, it's really hard to differentiate whether the mattress is broken or not. From the outside, a broken mattress looks just like a functional one. It took me some time to realize the central part of the mattress does not hold my back and my sleep quality was really bad during my stay. I thought the mattress was just of bad quality, but I never thought the mattress was left broken when I moved in.

I tried to argue with the property manager and tell her the mattress was already broken before I moved in and I didn't even know it was broken. I understood it was tenants' responsibility to report any damage beforehand, but how can a non-professinoal sleep tester tell the difference? I kept asking the property manager to show me the post move-out charge sheet of the previous tenant. If they didn't charge the previous tenant for breaking the mattress, it could well be a proof that I indeed broke the mattress. The property manager kept telling me they didn't review previous report upon inspection and refused to show me the report. It looks really fishy when they avoided answering my question.

Also, if I really broke the mattress, how come they only charge me 85 dollars? Are they just charging me 85 bucks and left the broken mattress there to cheat the next tenant? Or do they just buy an ill-quality mattress with 85 bucks and let it break by the next tenant?

To be honest the utility and environment of the apartments are satisfactory, but the management team is just not honest. You might think I just don't want to admit it's indeed me who broke the mattress, or I broke the mattress but I'm not aware of it. You might be right, but I have 4 other friends living in Capstone also telling me they have the same issue with the mattress but never suspected it's broken right when they moved in. What are the odds that so many people have the same problem?

I do agree with you regarding the importance of documenting any preexisting conditions in the apartment upon move in.  We instruct all of our residents to thoroughly inspect the apartment, complete the (provided) move-in inspection form and even take photos for your records.

I looked underneath using a flashlight (on my cell phone) and could clearly see the broken boards.  They are not hidden or covered, it is easy to see the interior of the box spring.  You would not need to be a "professional sleep tester" to see or feel the problem.  Since you did not note any problems when you moved in and nothing was brought to our attention regarding any issues with your bed, you were charged accordingly.  There was nothing "fishy" about this.  And yes, $85 is our cost for the box spring but a mattress or the set would have been more expensive.
In conclusion, because it was not reported when you moved in or during your lease term you were charged for the damage.  We provide all of the incoming residents with the instructions and paperwork to document any issues.  We are not able to repair or address issues that we are not made aware of.

review_text:
Had a terrible experience here for a few reasons:

Units are not cleaned before move in. I had a dirty floor and clogged kitchen and bathroom sinks when I moved to my unit. The dishwasher also was filled with water in the bottom after the first time I used it, and some sockets were damaged and the toilet lid was loose. This was despite the excessive cleaning (or repair) fees they often charge. I was charged 95 dollars after move out despite them coming into my apartment before moving out and telling me that it looked like I would owe 0 dollars. In general, maintenance is quite slow, at least after initial move in. It took a full month to get issues from move in resolved, and I know for some it took even longer.

There were also other disturbing issues outside my unit. There were multiple leaks (at least one from an electrical room) that soaked the carpet in the hallways between units, their electronic lock system would fail for some doors, while others would be permanently open, not requiring a key. A stairwell door was missing a doorknob once. The garage gate is permanently open (despite the fact that they issue parking fobs), and it took them more than 2 months to assign parking spots. The pool was never open despite the desk staff saying that they were confident it would be.

Desk/sales staff will give you inaccurate information about various policies such as what is included in a unit (there are NO ceiling lights/fans in the bedrooms in the units EXCEPT for the 1 bedroom STANDARD, NOT the more expensive 1 bedroom master) and whether parking can be cancelled/downgraded partway through a lease (as a warning, it cannot!). Make sure to get any promises in writing, as they will deny having ever made them if you follow up without explicit proof. Also, they arbitrarily change their availability of shorter than 12 month leases, while some of their staff denies the existence of their past availability. They will begin offering better deals for housing that begins in late August in early August, so wait to sign until then, at least if you do want a 12 month lease.

They mostly only offer tours of their model units, which are what I was impressed by and caused me to sign. As such, I highly recommend avoiding signing based off a model unit. There are definitely some nice things, such as the washer and dryer. The beds are queen, which is nice, but the mattresses are extremely firm and the bedrooms feel more cramped than they do on the tour. The shower felt smaller than in the tour, and would occasionally leak some water for no apparent reason which was a noise disturbance.

The noise level was better than at my old place, but it was still easily possible to hear loud noises such as generators and dog barking from the windows, loud rushing of water through pipes, and people talking in the hallways. I once heard loud noises from the unit above mine as well. In general, the apartment-to-apartment noise doesn't seem bad, although I suspect my wall neighbors were either unusually quiet or absent, and the noise from outside and water pipes easily makes up for it. Views are mostly good if you are on a higher floor, but you CANNOT be guaranteed to be off of the second floor under normal circumstances, where the views are either of a busy road, the interior walls of the building, a parking lot, or a run down house.

You can also clearly see the review manipulation done by management here on Google Reviews. Many of the five star reviews are uncannily similar, and often repeatedly mention a staff member, such as Jordan (Jai) Sneed, for no apparent reason. I can tell you from my experience that Jordan Sneed (the complex manager) threatened to refuse to approve a reletter (new tenant) for my unit if I was allowed to try a new unit (one of their vacant ones) in the complex first. I found this disturbing and unethical, and I'm disappointed that someone who is willing to threaten that is an apartment manager. My experience with the rest of the staff was somewhat better.

Overall, I cannot recommend against living here more.

*Honest, current resident review*

Meh, is all I can say about this apartment complex. Moving from LA, I was excited to see that luxury apartments were offered here. My fiancé and I signed a lease because it’s close for his work, and mine. We signed right when we arrived from LA. First mistake.

I thought it was great at first. Most of the staff that work here (NOW) are awesome, but other than that it’s: meh. Not that great.

Our first issue at the beginning was us signing the lease, the person working at the time told us we were good to go after telling us what to sign, and where to sign. A couple weeks after that, we had a thread of frantic emails and calls, saying that he needed us to sign another lease because he “accidentally” gave us a 6 month lease to sign, instead of a 12 month. After a week of annoyance, we signed all the papers again, and we didn’t know it was another lease agreement for 12 months, not another 6 months... so in total he had us sign two lease agreements adding up to 18 months. We agreed just for a 12 month lease (IN TOTAL), which he said it would be— it’s partially our fault for not reading what he sent over, and just signing it, but we just did because he said he would be able to fix it. But this issue bugged me so much, that it caused me to hate Latitude for the first 6 months of living here. I still have a grudge. (Tried to let it go, still can’t... ugh!).

The fire alarm was constantly going off, so annoying— like we get, stop forgetting your steak on the stove people! (LOL really, one of the fire alarms was because of that). The walls of Latitude are so thin that you can hear someone’s full conversation from the parking lot, on the 6th floor (and constant beeping from the trash), and don’t get me started on people that live below you or next to you! On Sunday’s the church rings their bells SO many times, and even with the window closed the rings are deafening. There was little to no hot water up until recently early in the mornings (I work until 7am). It was an issue when we lived on the 4th floor, we moved to the 6th, and I notified them of this issue (again) and it took over a week for our building to get notified that there was a water heater issue. (Yeah I was NOT happy showering in 54° water at the time— yes, we asked maintenance what the temperature of the water was when this issue first arose on the 4th floor). The internet is so spotty that I randomly disconnect at night, and is open for anyone and everyone to connect to (even though at first it was password protected). They got rid of the cable because they “upgraded” the internet. Just bleh, lame!

Oh! And the dog park, we went twice and never again. There was poop everywhere when we did: GROSS!

And did I mention when we lived on the 4th floor, we had a broken AC for the entire time we were there? When it was hot outside, our apt was at a constant 85° even after “fixing”. We got some credit (thanks) but... yikes.

* (This complaint below was resolved. Thanks Latitude— but still read incase this is an issue for you!)

* I’m one for my privacy and like being left alone. I love it, thrive in it, and since I work literally half of almost everyday: I live for it. But Latitude never can ever let us thrive in our own privacy. And so many emails. There’s always some sort of inspection, bug spray, stomping on the roof, always SOMETHING. I literally sleep all day once I get home from work (really bad habit, don’t attack me lol). Hospitals are overworked right now, and we are (almost) all working overtime— please just leave me alone. LOL. (And we pay so much rent for this, c’mon!).

Yeah, rent is also SO expensive here for what you get and deal with, comparable to LA! I did more research and found an apartment a little bit further (furnished, etc), with 2 bedrooms for $1000. Please do your research!

Super disappointing. I love most of the staff, which makes it a little better. But everything we had and have to deal with... uh.

2 stars given for the staff (shout out to Anthony & Elvin for always helping us), other than that: eeek.

The Amazing Leadership of Mr. Jordan Sneed and his team members is awesome. They get it -and understand how to provide quality service consistently -you are not a number but truly matter! Applauds for this group and leadership.

When I needed to move to one of their other properties mid-lease in order to help out a friend in dire straits, they were helpful and understanding. Same thing when the power company double-billed me, causing me to come up short for rent. Maintenence requests were always taken care of promptly and professionally. Making those requests online is easy, as is their online payment portal. Would definitely recommend, and would gladly lease from them again. I only wish more of their properties were dog friendly; had to find a different place that would accommodate my boyfriend's 70lb poodle.

I lived at Colonial Village for 2 years and never had a negative experience with management or the apartment. Several positive steps the management took: A week before I moved into what was supposed to be a 1 bedroom at a different complex, I got a call that the apartment had been vacated and was not in good condition, and they did not want to just cover up the problems with paint. I really appreciated their honesty, as I'm sure my experience would have been much different had they quickly tried to get that apartment in okay condition for me to move in. Instead, they offered me a larger apartment close by for the same price. The apartment itself was much more room than I needed, but was very comfortable and felt like home. I never had any run-ins with bugs or other pests, which was a huge plus for me. The few times I needed maintenance work, submitting a request online was simple and quickly taken care of, even on a Friday at 6 pm. At one point, my refrigerator stopped working, and it was replaced the same day, with no hassle. Paying rent online, as well, was simple and straightforward, never had issues. I was always notified in some way if maintenance workers were going to enter my apartment for any reason. Ultimately, I waited to leave a review until I got my deposit back, to see how it played out. A few weeks before I moved, I got emails stating exactly what management would look for upon issuing the deposit back, which I appreciated. I knew exactly what to clean, and ended up getting nearly all of my deposit back, which I thought was very fair. Overall, great experience. Thanks, R&B for giving me a place to live and always being straightforward and reasonable.

I had set up a date to tour an apartment a week prior to the tour date. I drove down five hours for them to tell me they leased the apartment without letting me know. The lady was anything but sympathetic to my situation. As I was voicing my concern about the meaningless drive, she didn't once take her eyes off her computer and then asked if I could move in a month later, despite starting my new job in a couple of weeks. I would steer clear of this place, there are much friendlier and professional housing services.

The RB Resident Services could not have come at a better time!  My spouse and I are expecting our first child very soon, and the services helped us with multiple hangings for the nursery and livingroom.  The cleaning service was exceptional!  The cleaning professional was on time and thorough!  Baby planning is overwhelming, so the convenience of not having to research home services was a relief!  Scheduling was quick and so was the service.  Also, we enjoyed the peace of mind the security of having “in house” services provided!  This is a definite win for the RB community!  Thank you!!!

Very nice apartment! Lots of space! I have a two bedroom two bathroom which is nice for guests and my extra belongings. Very quiet neighbors which is so important. The grounds crew keep the outdoors clean and snow removal is a plus. Any maintenance issues are handled quickly so that is a nice relief. I love living across the street from Kaufman Lake. I have a nice view and I enjoy many walks around the lake.

My family couldn't ask for a better place to live in Savoy. R&B truly seems to care about its tenants. The property is very well maintained. Maintenance requests are quickly responded to. We are so happy in our second year here!

I love everything R&B bring to the table when it comes to renting from them. They are super helpful when it comes to references for things. They always respond to any phone calls or emails you send. Maintenance men are out checking out the situation less then 24hrs from the time you requested maintenance. Staff is very upbeat and friendly. They offer so many things to help out people like myself who work 60 hours a week and cant run errands or find time to do anything and that is an A+  ALL AROUND..

I have been with Royse & Brinkmeyer since September 2018.
I was in the process of moving from my condo in Urbana and wanting to find a safe, clean, secure and comfortable place to live for my daughter and I. I found that in Royse & Brinkmeyer at Stonegate Village. The onsite property manager, Matt made sure I got what I needed and even went out his way to make sure I received 1st Floor preference. (something I've never had in my rental history) Katie was exceptionally patient and helpful when it was time to go apartment shopping. We looked at 3 properties before I fell in love with Stonegate Village and signed my lease! Stephanie and Kara really are a powerhouse when it comes to getting things done and filling in the gaps ! Cheyanne, Landon & Beth always come in clutch when anything tenant related is needed and exhibit amazing customer service just at the rest of the staff. Maureen is exceptional at working with tenants through hard times and finding formattable solutions for tenants with her years of expertise in finance and natural communication skills in that arena. Ed in Maintenence is ambitious about getting the job done as he has takin care of things in a timely fashion always. Shoutout the the entire maintenance staff and Pam as well ! The staff as a whole is excellent and I would recommend Royse & Brinkmeyer as the top pic and best value in Champaign County!!!

I have lived with Royse & Brinkmeyer for the past year and a half and have thoroughly enjoyed the experience! The complex I am at (Prairie Place) is well maintained, in a good location, and is a very affordable price. As a pet owner and someone who works in animal welfare, I am also very thankful for R&B’s leniency in allowing all of their tenants to own up to 2 cats. R&B had a lot of fun and creative activities they planned for their tenants as well, my favorites being a socially distanced outdoor movie in one of their empty lots and a community garden. Although I will no longer be living with Royse & Brinkmeyer in August, I definitely recommend those looking to rent in Champaign/Urbana to consider them.

I have been a tenant with Next Chapter Properties for 6 years before Royse and Brinkmeyer took over. I was very skeptical at first, as anyone would be, because of change where you are living. I finally addressed some major concerns I had with neighbors and our facility with Stephanie. She listed to my concerns and wasted no time fixing them. Two days ago I also was having problems with my smoke detectors chiming every 40 seconds, and Ed with maintenance was very kind, and walked me through how to get them to stop, so he could fix the problem in the morning while still making sure I was safe. I applaud Stephanie and Ed for their amazing customer service, and taking pride in what they do, and caring for their tenants.

I lived here for a year and after renting at 3 previous apartments before this one, I can easily say this is the WORST experience. Came to an apartment that wasn’t clean, left it spotless and they charged us $2,000 in repairs. The property upkeep is horrendous, the parking isn’t enough for how many people live there having to walk a block in the dark at night, the staff is rude and they do not provide assistance, they do not fix anything you complain about, and the area is NOT SAFE. Live anywhere else but here.

I was a recent long-time tenant of Royse and Brinkmeyer and if not for a relocation out of state, I still would be. I can't say enough good things about these folks...they are terrific landlords!!!
They are very sincere in their attitude, effort and services offered to those who rent from them. Their maintenance is unparalled in the CU community for it's responsiveness and courtesy. Royse and Brink is also very willing to work with and support their tenants...I truly came to appreciate that over the years as they helped me many times to find the perfect apts to fill my evolving housing needs.
Speaking of which, I have lived in several different properties and will share all were very well maintained down to mowing, regular cleaning and upkeep of laundry rooms and all common areas and snow removal. I was spoiled by the move-in/live-in condition of the apts...clean,clean,clean! And, Royse is super great about deposit refunds as long as you simply clean before you move out. They do not gouge tenants with suspect charges or fees of any kind and in terms of security deposits, they offer very clear guidlines to assure a maximum refund.
And as if all that were not enough, most importantly....the people are awesome!!! They are professional but also kind and personable...they truly want to help potential tenants find the perfect home. Shout-outs to Kara, Kaitie, Landon, Stephanie and Collin🌞🌞🌞🌞👌👌👌👍👍👍👍! They are trustworthy and very sincere. Unlike some other rental companies, I have never felt like I was being conned or upselled/hardselled by these folks.
I absolutely loved living in their properties. I never had to worry about whether or not a maintenance issue would be fixed, or if snow would be removed and knew that as my needs changed(sometimes at the last minute)they would be willing to work with me. If you truly want stress-free apartment living offered by good and honest people R&B can't be beat!!!!

Thank you everyone at Royse & Brinkmeyer....you guys are truly the best!!!!!🌞

Royce & Brinkmeyer are the very best company to rent from hands down! You will find they are 1st class all the way making your experience with them the best.
You will find all of their rentals clean, safe and well taken care of. They do their best always listening, and constantly making improvements.
All their staff  are first rate. Always respectful, courteous,  and easy to reach. They respond quickly when you contact them.They even have a resident portal.
You will never be caught with unknown surprises, and they don't have to run contest with their employees to get fake ratings to coverup low ratings.
Two of my adult children rented from them and had great experiences. When they moved out they received all their deposit back.
This is a family who really cares about being real and making your experience the best it can be.

I was honestly happy living at Stonegate Village for nearly 4 years. Maintenance was always really good - got a new air conditioner and new dishwasher the next day after I put in maintenance requests. They were also pretty good about extending my lease when I needed to for periods shorter than one year.

However, when I moved out I cleaned my apartment pretty well, and I got an itemized list of charges for cleaning, which supposedly cost more than the $800 security deposit. They charged $20 to "clean" the brand new dishwasher mentioned earlier that had been used no more than 5 times, among other charges for "cleaning" things that were thoroughly cleaned. My advice: either don't clean when moving out because you'll be charged anyway or take pictures and fight it so you won't be grossly overcharged.

Have stayed in Champaign area for almost 9 years and moved many times to find a reasonable priced apartment which fits my needs (i.e. safe and quiet during the night, move-in date with some flexibility, prompt responding to any question or maintenance needs). Royse and Brinkmeyer Apt has met all my needs and definitely is the best landlord I have had in addition to University School Housing. Their staff in office is always welcoming, friendly, courteous, and helpful. Their maintenance crew is responsible and did a good job. For example, they shoveled the snow in a reasonable pace during snow days. They even provided snow melt and emailed winter alert/tips to their tenants, which was helpful to me as a person from the tropical zone. They maintain the property quite well; I remembered the apartment was really clean when I moved in. They have transparent leasing terms and payment plan, and also accommodate my move-in/out need as much as possible without asking for a fortunate. I have been really happy with their management.

Royse & Brinkmeyer provides the best apartment I’ve lived in for years! I’ve been at their Prospect Point site for about a month. When I moved in it was nearly flawless, spotlessly clean, new carpet, new floors, freshly painted walls… They fixed the couple of tiny issues I fussed about in two or three days. The area is quiet; there is enough parking to invite friends over (unlike my previous neighborhood). I love the floor plan of this particular apartment, two bedrooms, two full bathrooms, kitchen, laundry, living/dining/office area and several closets.

When I first started renting the management was very helpful and friendly when I requested a new apartment because of noisy upstairs neighbors. Now that my property manager has switched I can't say the same. I moved out of state for a job and had just resigned a lease 24 hours prior and thought with a minimal fee they would let me out but I was wrong. Fast track 6 months and I'm still trying to find someone to sublease while they let it sit vacant because I'm still responsible for rent. During the whole sublease process they haven't been helpful just reciting the same information in emails and when I call.

The staff is amazing here. Anytime I have called they have been very prompt in responding even after hours. I really enjoy renting from them and they make you feel very comfortable when calling to tall about any issues you may have. The staff is very helpful, understanding and caring. I was very lucky to have found such a great company to rent from.

I am revising my review from what I originally posted. Management reached out to me same day as I posted my original post to identify and look into solving my problem. Since the entire issue, has been resolved professional and swiftly with my security deposit. It is unfortunate, currently when disputing a security deposit the only way is snail mail, but they are looking into improving contact methods.
Overall, from the issue I had aside. I enjoyed my year that I lived at Prospect Pointe. The apartment was as it showed in the photos when I was choosing. Maintenance was good at fixing the couple issues that I did have. Management was friendly and helpful when I switched to a garage closer to my apartment when it opened up. Plenty of room and really liked the layout of the emerald. Parking was great, I always had ample room so you could be far enough away from other vehicles that you would not have to worry about door dings and stuff like that. The location was extremely convenient with the savoy plaza across the street and Walmart just a mile down the road.
My reason for moving on was the lack of amenities and high cooling bills in the summer. Every electric bill in the summer was 120 minimum (could have been because I was on the top floor?). In my opinion, the value for what I was getting with the raise of rent on my lease renewal was not competitive to other places in the same price range.

I lived at Stonegate almost two years. Nice property but not much parking on the west side.  The office was flexible about my move-out date, which was great since I had some travel around that time.
Maintenance was timely. Downside was the apartment was on the top floor and the electric bill in the summer was nuts.
They returned most my deposit, which was quite fair.  Would rent from them again if needed.

My overall experience with Royse and Brinkmeyer has been severely underwhelming. I have repeatedly tried working with Katie, senior leasing agent, but she has proven to be deliberately deceptive, condescending, and insensitive.
The unit I was shown poorly represented the one that I later received. My cabinet facings were taped onto the kitchen cabinets, rather than properly repaired, or replaced. When I patiently reported the issue, I was neglected for months, only to be later told that there was no resolution because the cabinets were “too old”.
I foolishly agreed to renew the lease if a rental discount was offered, and that negotiation was a dispute on its own. Katie verbally informed me that the full discount would be applied immediately, but later claimed that the discount would only be honored months later when the renewal kicked in.
When tenants who blasted bass speakers and violently argued at all hours of the night moved in next door, Katie instructed me to continue calling the police because “nothing could be done on her end”. She merely offered “walk-bys”, typically reporting back that nothing was heard at the time of her visit.
Despite the respect and accountability that I have demonstrated as a tenant, even now during a global pandemic, the team at Royse & Brinkmeyer continues to lack empathy and reasoning. I am needing to end my lease to move back home due to personal COVID-19 related family matters, but of course I cannot be accommodated. I offered to find a new tenant if the company would grant a name transfer on the lease, but this was refused. The impractical and unfeasible options that I have been presented with are not even offered on the lease, so I am puzzled by the refusal to compromise.
I hope that by sharing this information, I can prevent prospective tenants from experiencing similar frustration and disappointment.

I've had an excellent tenant experience with R & B. My apartment is spacious and affordable. I haven't had any serious maintenance issues and the minor requests that I have made have been addressed right away. The neighbors and office staff are very friendly. The laundry facility is well maintained.

Management and apartments are decent, however they will charge you up the ass for petty stuff. Got locked out of my apartment once and they charged me $75 to get back into my own place! After moving out, not only did they keep my $600 deposit, but they charged me an addition $60 for petty cleaning expenses that didn't make any sense! I kept my apartment in great condition, there is no way it costs $480 to clean a small, one bedroom apartment. And if you sign up to use you apartment as a show model, expect visits 3x a day, everyday with about a 10 minute warning in advance. In addition, don't expect any assistance from maintenance. My heater wasn't working in the winter and I practically froze to death; I ended up having to buy a space heater to keep myself warm. Maintenance was unhelpful and took way too long to fix the problem. They clearly didn't want to help me out and had a snarky attitude while doing so, and management did nothing when I reported this issue. This place is a joke, definitely would not recommend!

I began renting with them right out of high school, and rented with them for three years. I had to move away for school for two years but am moving back and I knew I wanted to come back to Royse and Brinkmeyer. They were always incredibly kind, professional, and responded quickly to any maintenance work i needed done. I would and have recommended them to anyone looking for a place in Champaign/Savoy.

I've had three leases with Royse and Brinkmeyer and been extremely happy with all of them. They have a wide variety of apartments at all price points and take incredible care to help you find the one that you're looking for. I would recommend them to anyone looking for a clean, responsive, attentive property management company.

I have lived with Royse & Brinkmeyer since I first arrived in Champaign-Urbana over 5 years ago! They are a great company who is very responsive and who deeply care about their residents. I only have positive things to say about them and I plan to stay with them until I move out of town!

I just left an apartment managed by this company after living here for 1 year. I have nothing but positive things to say about them. Over the course of the year, I have had 0 issues with the management. We had an issue in our complex where packages were being stolen. Once reported, the management quickly offered a package holding service free of charge as well as made our buildings more secure. This was a quick and appropriate reaction and really representative of the way management works.

I also had an issue where I misread the lease and forgot my move-out date (my fault, entirely). Management worked closely with me to make sure everything was handled including refunding my overpayed rent the very next day. They even apologized that they couldn't do more!

While living in the apartment, the few issues I had with the apartment were quickly addressed by their kickass maintenance crew.

Upon move-out, my security deposit was payed within 2 weeks with a fully itemized list of very reasonable charges (I drilled a ton of holes for shelves and they charged me for painting over the spots). I was pleasantly surprised after having dealt with other management companies that nickle-and-dimed my security deposit.

I'm sure that my pleasant experience was because I, as a tenant, exhibited some common sense. When in doubt, I always called management before I did anything to the apartment (example: the ton of holes). I'm sure this really smoothed over relations since I could get a sense of how they expected me to keep the apartment. If you ever have any questions, I'd suggest giving them a call. It could avoid a nasty surprise later on.

All in all, Royse and Brinkmeyer deserve every star I've given them for their common sense and courtesy as a management company. I'd highly recommend them over the other student leasing companies in this town.

During the winter storm when wind chills reached below -40, despite doing everything I could, my pipes froze. Emergency maintenance came within 20 minutes and thawed my pipes immediately. He also fixed a water pressure issue I had since I moved in but never worried about since it was just one of the sinks. As a single mom with 3 kids and having absolutely no knowledge of how to repair anything, I was so grateful for how amazing this maintenance man was. He was even incredibly nice and polite to my kids.

I'd like to rate them "ZERO" star if i could. This is one of the WORST apartments company in town. I've lived in continental plaza for two years. Our apartment's window was broken into a complete lack of security and interest in safety putting my family at risk. Despite the fact that we hand them over the Police report we end up being charged repair and rescreen fees against our deposit after we left. They fail to proctect my family but they decide to charge us for their mistakes. Their maintenance team is just horrible. I had to call multiple times in order to get a leaking sink fixed. They even not able to fix it properly. Don' t even expect you'll get anything back from your deposit. They make sure to charge you anything they come up with even if you did your best to get the apartment clean and fresh. I DO NOT RECOMMEND AT ALL TO RENT TO THESE GUYS, YOU WILL END UP ROBBED.

18 months at Stonegate Village. Very satisfied renting from R&B. Office personal were always professional, helpful and friendly. Any issues we had were addressed promptly. Neighbors were friendly and noise from other units was never a problem. Plenty of parking too! Absolutely would have stayed longer if the house we bought had not come available.

I have lived at the Ginger Creek Apartments for 4 years. The first two were fine, I did not have any issues. The last 2 have been a nightmare.

I am currently trying to move out of Ginger Creek Apartments at the moment because Royce & Brinkmeyer are unwilling to provide any assistance in helping to keep myself or my vehicle safe.  My car has been broken into 3 times in a year and a half.  The police have said my vehicle seems to be targeted.  It took Royce & Brinkmeyer 2 weeks to get back to me on renting a garage.  In fact I had to call several times without them calling me back.  TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!  Still I had to argue back and forth to get them to take $15/month off a garage and they said I couldn't move into one until June 25.  My car was broken into on the 1st.

Unfortunately, even with a police report or dispatch reports this company DOES NOT VALUE THE SAFETY of their tenants.

I spoke with someone just this morning who rented from this agency 15 years ago and they too had nothing but terrible things to say in regards to working with these people.  They seem to only care if your rent is in on time.

I don't understand these people at all they told me my credit was bad. I've never had an eviction in my life I always pay my rent on time and always keep my place clean.they're going to go buy my bad credit I have good credit with all the landlords I've ever been with. I know some landlord we're skeptical me  because of my bad credit but they never regretted it.just because somebody has bad credit doesn't mean they don't pay the rent on time or their other bills.

Three years ago we wanted to rent an Apartment so we thought we could ask for availability. I was going through divorce. This company did a background check and they came back asking weird personal questions. I couldn’t forget and and my credit report didn’t their rude behavior after three years.
I had a horrible experience with this company!

Leasing Agent Jess was very helpful in helping us find a place to stay. She stayed in contact with us during our decision making process and informed us all of the options that they had available. They had everything and more for what we were looking for in a place to stay. I will recommend them to others.

I renewed my lease and tried out a different apartment complex. It is not in a safe area. I have been here for two weeks and my car has attempted to be broke into. I also locked myself out of the building on a Sunday chasing my toddler and letting go of the door, I call emergency maintenance to see if anyone can let me in after trying to buzz neighbors and they tell me they refuse to help and will have to pay for a locksmith. It’s been a nightmare so far. I regret resigning my lease. Thank GOD I signed a shorter one.

I would never recommend “Royse & BrinkMeyer Apartments.” I started a lease with a different company in 2014 and Royse took over mid-2016. When they took over, they claimed that because they were a bigger company than the one before; thus, they would be more proactive and that their maintenance team would be “fast” than the previous company (one-person maintenance). Royse never lived up to that promise. The first time I called maintenance for them to fix some issues with the apartment (screen door, insulation, etc.), they never responded “quickly” as they claimed. It took them over 6 months to take care of the maintenance issues. Also, Gabriela Villasenor (lease agent) was not much help when I needed her. In addition, the landscape at Misty Cove (Royse owns several townhomes in the area) was not kept well since they took over. The previous company that managed the townhomes in the area at Misty Cove - with one person (Mike) doing the maintenance - did a better job keeping the landscape of the place than the Royse’s “fast” maintenance team. If you happen to rent, be aware of the “cleaning” fees they would charge at the end of the lease; there is a long list of possible fees. Their expectation is that the house is “deep” cleaned! Although my townhouse was clean – and there were no stains or major issues, it was not as clean as to meet their expectation (I left with the feeling that they won’t clean the house before another tenant moves in, so make sure you leave the house “spotless” clean). To give you an idea, the kitchen and bathroom floors had some small debris in the corners that I missed (charged $80). Some of the cleaning fees were fairly charged (but not fairly valued; e.g., left plastic bags and bag of rice in one cabinet by mistake, so they had to throw it away, but I was charged $45 for that massive man power!), but there were others – based on my experience from other management – should have never been added.  For instance, there were some cleaning issues behind the toilet that they found, that I could not see before I left; otherwise, I would have taken care of (charged $95). I did not complain about these final fees because I preferred to be charged for something like that than dealing with this management. Based on my experience with Royse, I would stay away from this management.

Leasing agent Jess was awesome in showing and explaining details about everything. She made me feel comfortable and actually part of the Royse Brinkmeyer family. She was prompt and organized. I would def recommend her and the company to anyone. Thank you so much

I had to rent the apartment without visiting and it was in worst conditions than showed in the pictures. Once in, they didn’t want to do any work because “it’s what you get for the price you are paying”. The deposit they require is much higher than in other properties (in my case, about 10 times more). When I moved to another place, they charged me a crazy amount for ridiculous reasons. After some complaining, they agreed to give me back some more money. Even though, I kept being charged for some damages and some dust that were already in the property when I first moved in. Only positive aspect is the management during the rental period.

I have lived with Royse throughout my time in law school (3 years).  I signed with them because they seemed to really care about their residents and they had the cleanest apartments I saw.  That held true during my stay with them in Champaign.  They were always responsive to requests and checked on my apartment while I was out of town.  Overall, i could not ask for a better leasing company during my time in Champaign.

The staff are very friendly and helpful. Maintenance is always quick to fix any problems that come up. Stonegate Village is a great place to live, there are spacious apartment layouts at affordable prices. Theres a pool, secure entrances to my building, and laundry facilities.

I have been with them for a whole year, Maintenance is bad, they come to your place, enter, and don't even leave a note.

The laundry is for the 2 apartments, but only one is in charge of paying for water and power.

They were very sneaky when signing the lease, after you signed and paid the deposit, then they will tell you about the extra laundry agreement, which basically you don't have a choice....

In our contract says that they will take care of snow, and provide salt,.... we still never got salt, and our drive way still has snow!

I could keep going... but you get the point... watch out!

I lived at 2 of their apartments and they were always great about fixing things.  The itemized list of what they will charge you for your deposit is annoying, but if you clean what is on the list, you get it back.  It was off-putting, but at least you know what you will be charged if you don't clean the fireplace, oven, etc.  It is all itemized, so if people are complaining about not getting their money back, they didnt clean what was on the itemized checklist or just destroyed the apartment.

I am impressed with Royse & Brinkmeyer as a leasing company! I had a fantastic experience with Jess showing me around. She was genuinely interested in helping me find exactly what I was looking for in an apartment down to the unit based on my preferences.

As a long term renter in CU since 1987, a blessing to have a stable, well managed, private landlord in heart of C-U with professional and responsive maintenance since 2006. R&B cares about and invests in the local community. Only more obvious during this pandemic.

Before you end your leasing terms your leasing agents wiil show visitors your apartment anytime during their work hours without making sure that you are aware of it in advance.  They are not even willing to ensure that the visitors will take off shoes or wear shoe covers before they enter your room.  They have little(in their own words, an amount of) respect for their tenants.

My leasing agent, Matthew Raab has been very helpful with facilitating my move.  He's always available to respond to my calls, texts and questions.  He's very informative and accommodating to all my needs.  I am looking forward to living @ THE ASPEN.

I have lived with Royse and Brinkmeyer for ~17 years now and have loved leasing with them.  If there is a maintenance issue; they fix it promptly and professionally; if there is a domestic issue; it is handled with dignity and understanding.  There's no place else I would rather live or lease from.

I have rented from Royse & Brinkmeyer since 1991. Obviously they must be doing something right if I have been a tenant so long. Their maintenance department is very good, quick to respond. The people overall are friendly.

Very impressed and satisfied with R&B. They were very accommodating to my needs. Neal was very responsive in assisting me with any concerns or requests that I had.  Would definitely rent with them again.

Almost a perfect place to live in. Love the furniture, the design and very good maintenance! Convenient location to preschool, supermarket, Imax theater, and restaurant. Love the BBQ place and walking trail nearby.
Two problems:
1. The noise is a little bit loud. We can hear our neighbors.
2. Don't have an on-site gym!

Quiet place to live. Maintenance responds fast to your requests. Property is well maintained. Onsite property manager is a huge plus. No more phone calls or a trip across town. You can just walk into the office right on site.

Don't rent here if you want to get any of your deposit back!  I left my apartment cleaner than when I got it and they took some of my deposit for "painting" when the lease stated that touch-ups were free for only renting apartment for 1 year. Tried talking with management about it and they never even sent me a final letter back.

As of now, I have just searched for apartments and just signed my new lease... but so far so great! Kaitie has been extremely helpful through all of this and has really listened to what I'm looking for in an apartment. She has made this process very easy and painless, I cannot wait to move into my new apartment!

Stonegate Village,
Safe and quite to live in, for us wise. Was very happy and proud until Rosye Brinkmeyer nickel and dime us for our deposit. We have made sure our apartment was clean before we left, as it was our very first apartment as a family. A sentimental place for us but at the end they took my satisfaction. 80% of our deposit was taken. SERIOUSLY???? review_text:
Many of the reviews on here are from West Quad employees, so I'll be 100% honest about living here. I lived at WQ the 2015-16 school year, and there are definitely some positives and negatives.

Positives:

The amenities are great. There is a nice gym (with a sauna) which we got plenty of use out of. The outdoor space with the volleyball court, grills, pool, hot tub, and jumbotron were awesome. Not many apartment buildings have things like this. The staff was also willing to put things on the jumbotron if you asked. When it was nice out in August, September, April, and May, this area was packed, and was usually a lot of fun.

The apartment was also pretty nice. The furniture is modern and somewhat comfortable. The kitchen is spacious and is really nice. We had basically no problems with the appliances. I lived with three roommates (4x4 unit) and we often had friends over and we still had more than enough room for everyone. The apartment is definitely big enough. The bathrooms are also big. We each had our own bathroom and shower, which not many college students have the luxury of. The bedrooms are definitely big enough. I had the smallest style of room West Quad has (I think) and in addition to the full size bed and desk that come with the room, I was able to fit my TV stand, TV, small cabinet, guitar, and amp in only about half of the room. I have no real complaints about the apartment itself.

Negatives:

I cannot understate this... This place can get very, very loud. I'm convinced that they screwed up something with the walls during construction, because they are paper thin. You can hear anything going on outside, even just conversations. And I'm not talking about only outside in the hallway, I'm also talking about outside the building. It often sounded like there was no wall at all. The people that party here not only on the weekends, but also during the week, can get so obnoxiously loud that you cannot fall asleep. Many of the people making all the noise aren't even students, they are townies.

I understand, this is a college town, people party and it can get loud. But this was over the top. People blasting music out of giant speakers in their cars at full volume with the bass all the way up in the driveway of the building at 3 AM on a Wednesday night is not normal. Literally my room would be shaking. Just constantly people yelling, fighting, and blasting obnoxious music ALL. NIGHT. LONG. It's horrible, and management does nothing about it because they know that if they stepped in and took action and made an effort to control the noise, people would live somewhere else.

Also, the day before finals started, WQ decided to have a full on rock concert in the courtyard all afternoon, so there's that. I love loud concerts, but not the day before finals outside my window.

The ventilation in the hallways is horrible. People would smoke out there all the time, and the smell would linger for days. There was one time when we could smell the smoke in our kitchen.

West Quad advertised that the building would be a private community, but literally anyone can basically walk right in. People often put things like bricks or floor mats in front of the doors on the side of the building, so how is it a private community?

One minor note: the manager (Brian) told me he would help me out to collect information about West Quad's construction for a class assignment. He told me to pick a time in a certain week, and when I went to the office to make the plans in person (because he was slow to respond to my emails) I found out he was actually on vacation that entire week. He then completely ignored my attempts to set up a meeting, leaving me to scramble to find someone else to gather information from in the couple days before the assignment was due.

If obnoxious people do not bother you, you'd probably enjoy West Quad. The building itself is very nice and the amenities are great. My roommates and I just could not stand the noise any longer and chose somewhere else for next year.

review_text:
I’ve lived here for almost 2 years and have renewed for next year. The bad reviews on here seem more like personal issues and not full reviews of the apartment building so let me give you one.

The apartment: When I moved in it was clean and the process was seamless. They even left you a little welcome goodie bag. The view is amazing on any floor and overall it’s a very quiet building.

The maintenance: Brain is the best and truly wants the building to be functioning smoothly. Per the elevator review, we had a problem with our elevators breaking, maintenance said pushing the door open/close button can cause them to fail. As someone who takes the elevator about 15 times a day to let my dog out, I can tell you people push that button like it’s spitting out money every time. The doors have a timer, we are all going somewhere, wait an extra 3 seconds.
For mandatory things like filter changes or walk through, we get ample notification time and they are quick and polite. My work orders are always completed quickly and I feel like maintenance actually cares about how things are working in my apartment. The building is also always so clean. When they clean our hallway floors it smells amazing!!

The Staff: Everyone who works here is extremely nice and always says hi to me! I’ve never had a problem with them and they are always willing to help. I also love all the different events they put on like giving out food and social events.
One time my door fob detector thing died when I had my dog out at 6 in the morning. I called the emergency line and they had someone there to replace the batteries in 15 minutes.

The amenities: I use the gym almost everyday and never have not been able to use a machine. It’s clean and has a variety of weights, machines and cardio equipment. They even have a room where you can do fitness classes or yoga. Our package room is awesome because you get a text when a package arrives and you can go in there 24/7. This is really nice because you know the package is safe and don’t need to rush home.

Overall, take negative reviews with a grain of salt. I’ve lived here and have been very comfortable.

We really appreciate you evenly weighing your full experience here at Burnham, and what's more, renewing for the year to come. review_text: They are bad with records and do not keep promises. It has been over a month since I moved out; by now my security deposit should have been mailed to me (or at least should have been notified as to why they are delayed). This is more of a concern now because I have to pay for the carpet and kitchen cleaning I got charged for (which I don't mind, I didn't clean it that well anyways) but if I don't get my security deposit back to pay for the cleaning, then Burnham could report it to a bill collector to affect my credit score. I went in to talk to the leasing office and they couldn't tell me explicitly what was going on. The best they could tell me was that the system was down: kept details to a minimum, didn't tell me since when it was down, didn't tell me when it would be back up, and made other excuses as to why I couldn't get my deposit back. If this system is down I do not understand how the records for current tenants are being kept (so be weary all you who are living there right now). Normally I would be willing to be patient for matters like this but there are horrible reviews online about how Burnham has consistently lied to their tenants about security deposits. (check for yourself on yelp) I have also heard from friends who have lived here that they do not reward referrals at all (even though they advertise that they will be rewarded with giftcards). I am disappointed because I had an overall nice experience living here. The staff were always very friendly and the place was kept clean. I'm sad to write this review since on a surface level, this apartment is great. I like my room layout, the furnishings, and the amenities. I wish the kitchen was bigger but the reason why this place gets a 1 star is due to the copious water issues throughout the past year, and the infrequent hot water that residents get. Whoever designed this building and the management responsible for maintaining it have failed to account for the needs of residents when it comes to water.

There have been instances where management have been aloof or straight up missing when there was no hot water in the building, with ice cold water coming from the tap, shower, and faucets. Getting hot water requires you leaving on the shower for more than 15 minutes, making it extremely inconvenient when you want a fast shower. In some cases, I have left my water on for 45 minutes with no hot water reaching my shower. It's always a gamble for hot water, sometimes you can get lucky and can get hot water in 5 minutes, other times you are waiting an hour. It's a waste of water and extremely disruptive to my daily schedule.

Management has promised a permanent solution is incoming but until that is apparent, this review will stay up. I have still not forgiven them for not putting an emergency number up when they closed the office down once for training and hot water for the entire building was not available for 8 hours.  I hope this gets resolved soon in the form of management reducing rent payments or compensating us in another manner because this has been ridiculous.

Update: it’s been a year but i never received any compensation for my issues. Because of this, I have left the review on here

review_text:
Overall, I'd say that the overall experience here is subpar/acceptable, at the very least. Although the amenities such as the gym, basketball courts, and pool are pretty nice, those are all that I can think of as being "good". During my period living here, there have been so many issues/red flags. Hopefully, my review can help you rethink and really consider if this is the place that you will want to stay at.

My main concerns come as issues with Seven07 management. In my opinion, they have not been doing a good job at all keeping up with resolving any of the tenants' issues. There was the whole no-hot water situation, where they did the absolute absolute bare minimum to stay within regulations and not get into any trouble. In the first few days where there was no hot water, nothing was done at all. As residents were frustrated with the lack of action, some decided to speak with the Champaign-Urbana Tenant Union, and discuss legal options to resolve the issue. Strangely and interestingly enough, the next day, Seven07 staff put out a notice that they would be implementing a shuttle service to take residents to ARC for showers. It seems quite obvious that they are doing the bare minimum to not get sued, and won't take action unless forced to. Also, they supposedly voted to not provide compensation for the lack of hot water, even though it is clearly on them for not resolving the issue in a timely fashion. I can understand that they want to reduce the overhead and maximize margins, but I will just say this now, they may have "saved costs" but at the expense of their tenants' trust. I, along with others, have sent numerous emails asking for details about the compensation and at the time of this writing, over three months have passed, and not a single word has been said. They are trying to brush this off and hope residents forget about it, which goes to show how much they care about your experience as a tenant. One other thing that is indicative of poor management is how they also handle the persistent internet issues. Even though residents from all over the building are reporting the same, consistent issues with the internet connection being spotty, they still want each individual resident to call the internet service provider. Logically speaking, if residents from literally almost every part of apartment are experiencing similar internet connectivity issues, I think that it might just be a larger problem here. It seems that they just do not want to put in the effort to fix these problems.
**My concerns with the management team do not extend to any of the student members. They have been doing a great job, and are always friendly and willing to help.

If Seven07 reads this, and decides to post the same comment saying that I should contact their office, please know that I have already sent numerous emails, and have never gotten a response. I hope to keep this review up to share my experience and provide a different perspective on what leasing an apartment here would entail.

I NEVER get hot water here. This has been an issue since the beginning of the school year in August 2021. Fast forward to February 2022 and it’s gotten much worse. It’s freezing cold water! There have been instances where I’ve had to shower in the cold water because I had no choice. People have things to do, and worrying about hot water is BY NO MEANS one of those things.
I’ve set up work orders to get it fixed last year and a few weeks ago when I came back in January after break. They came around 4 days after I submitted my work order, and then when they came nothing changed. I also called management but that hasn’t changed anything. I spoke to the leasing manager Brian, and he just asked me why I didn’t place a work order before. First of all, I did place work orders before and second of all, that doesn’t solve my problem. I’m having this problem for a long time, so I would obviously call you. They just tell you the following things from their laundry list of responses: turn your water on for 30 minutes, no one else is having this issue, it’s the weather’s fault. Yeah right. My roommates and I have left the water on for more than 30 minutes and that does NOT do anything (not to mention that it’s a waste of water). With the winter storm, they found out that they need replacement parts for the boiler system. That should’ve been checked well in advance so that this problem wouldn’t arise again in the first place. What’s funny is that the management wasn’t even in the building when there was a cold water outage for us in November because of a shift in management. They have a track record of leaving the building when something goes wrong. Oh, and don’t get me started on the weekly fire alarms, one of them being at 6 am. I absolutely do NOT recommend living here as it is not worth taking showers in freezing cold water. Save your money and find another place.

I definitely don’t think tower is worth the money and I won’t be living here again after this school year. It’s still a big step up from living in dorms and I would choose tower over Snyder any day. However, if you compare it to the other apartments in champaign, T3 is on the low low end. The building looks dope from the outside and the lobby looks good too, but the units themselves are ugly and outdated. I don’t think that T3 deserves a 1 star rating; maybe 2-3 but I felt it was necessary to give this place 1 star to offset all of the fake reviews people put on here to get free food.

review_text:
Living at the Tower at Third (T3) was overall an enjoyable experience. My favorite part is the amenities. The study lounge, laundry room, and gym facilities all require a key to get into, and thus they feel secure at all times.

The study lounge overall is incredibly comfortable and aesthetically pleasing with a modern look. The small study rooms in the lounge have housed many late-night study and movie sessions with friends (they have a TV in each of the three mini rooms). Definitely one of the few apartments on campus that offers free printing services.

Regarding the laundry facilities in the basement, I've rarely had to wait to put my laundry in the washer or dryer. And the machines don't require coins, which is a plus. Overall, the basement and main floor are very sophisticated and give T3 a luxury feel.

In terms of the rooms themselves, T3 has undergone the process of renovating them. Last school year, our old brown carpet was renovated with stylish gray hardwood flooring (and our rent stayed the same!), so it seems like many positive changes are happening.

The bedrooms felt roomy and include a spacious closet, dresser, desk, and chair. (The dresser also included a large attached mirror when I lived there in 2019-2020, but that may have changed since.) Depending on which direction you're facing, this apartment can have great views. (Picture attached.) I enjoyed living on a lower floor (5th) because it meant less waiting in the elevator when people from all floors were trying to get on in the morning. Also, all utilities are included, so you can expect a consistent rent each month!

I also enjoyed the convenience - T3 is less than a ten-minute walk from the Union. It's also one block away from the 22N/S and 13S bus lines. It's also minutes away from Walgreens and Green Street in general.

Also, packages are delivered straight to the leasing office on the main floor, so it's easy to pick them up. Having the leasing office in the same building makes picking up packages, paying rent, and asking questions very convenient.

The staff is also helpful and kind. Melissa, Jasmine, and Suha are the staff that I've had the pleasure to interact with, and all have been understanding and accommodating.

I would live there again if I could, and I would recommend this apartment building to anyone that wants to live in a comfortable, cozy place. Thanks for the experience!!

review_text:
The tower at third has changed a lot in the past few years with the transition in management (hence the 4 star review, the first 6 months of the two year lease were up in the air, but the Tower has redeemed itself!). Maintenance is responsive and polite, and they always notify you when they have scheduled maintenance inspections and are prompt for requests. Tower is not as nice as their sister property aesthetically (Suites at Third) but that’s because I moved in before they could replace some of the finishings in Tower in 2017; not the complex’s fault. It also is priced knowing that Suites is considered a more luxury property.  For what the units are at Tower, the apartments are priced pretty competitively for the surrounding area to have shared laundry and gym and mail all in the basement and the security guards are an added plus. The students in the office also work hard to do right by you and your requests (shout out to Caleb and Cyrus!) and they’re always smiling no matter how many packages you have delivered in one week (another great service!) the only downside: the elevators are down a lot but I’ve never had to walk up the nine flights to my room, just wait longer for an elevator, and sometimes the hallways have an odor, but it doesn’t affect your unit with the door closed. It’s an older building: it has its quirks like that. I’ve found it a pleasure to live in, as I don’t need “luxury” to eat, sleep, and do my studies. It’s a nice, simple property that checks all the boxes and then some!

TL;DR I have always gotten help here when asked, the rooms function for great living and socializing, and Melissa and American Campus Communities have really turned this property around since 2017. I would recommend you live here if you want to live off campus, but a short walk away from anything (also go Caleb and Cyrus!)

I would not recommend this place to anyone. My room mate and I have had countless negative experiences from the start. For one, THE WINDOWS DO NOT OPEN. This is not something they mention during tours and it is such an inconvenience, especially since the smoke alarm goes off all the time. Our air conditioning and heating was constantly broken, and without windows the place felt trapped all the time. We have had so many issues with utilities as well, and the office was never really helpful. Another problem was, A LACK OF HOT WATER. We have called countless times about issues with getting hot water, and it is ridiculous that at 725 a month we are told that we have to let it run for 30 minutes, which by the way barely worked. The building advertises overnight security, but for a majority of the year there was barely anyone there and the doors used to always be unlocked. For the price, this place is absolutely not worth it. It needs a major renovation and a way nicer office staff.

review_text: On my second semester here. My favorite part is that the laundry room and gym are within around 50 feet from my door when I take the elevator. Both laundry and gym are kept very clean and functional. Staff is great, apartments are great, great location. I'll probably be spending another year here.

I have been living here for over 2 years which I believe is a testament to how much I have enjoyed my time here. Onsite maintenance completes work in a timely fashion and the management personnel are very easy to work with. Building has security guard at front door overnight. The amenities include a new gym, free laundry, study rooms, and a game lounge with pool table and ping pong. Apartment cost is very reasonable and includes unlimited electricity, water, and cable/internet service. T3 has a great location, just one block off Green Street, and just over a quarter mile from the quad. Would highly recommend living here.

My daughter is a student at U of I and lived here the 2013/2014 school year.  She really liked it and i absolutely loved it as a parent.  I felt she was completely safe there.  They did a really good job with her roommate matching and picked someone similar to her.  Everything is included in the rent. You don't have to worry about paying for extras like heat, air conditioning, cable, internet, water.  They have a huge laundry room and it's all free.  There is no cap to the electric like at alot of places.  She could make her apt as cool or as warm as she wanted to. She had a deluxe apt which i think it well worth the extra money. review_text: Soso

I lived at 1008 S 4th St this last year and had a truthfully terrible experience. The biggest issue of all is their poor management. This is probably the worst flaw to have when the leasing office isn’t located in the building. Getting a hold of them for anything was far too difficult. If I called during their hours, no one would answer. Even if I were to visit, no one was there to receive me. Also, they had a very poor demeaner both over the phone and in person. Their lack of respect for residents became even clearer when our unit was sold without directly informing us. When I went to renew my lease, I was told that I would be able to do so, until only a moment later, the bedspace was sold.
Another example: the thermostat was cranked by inspectors to 83-85°F during winter break without us knowing, ultimately increasing the utility bill to the highest it’d ever been, during the months we’d been present the least. When we called for an explanation, we were told that they had possibly done that because we had probably placed the temperature too low…so the only possible course of action in their minds was to increase the temp by 20°F. Not sure how that makes sense or why it’s my problem.
Another example: the only elevator in the entire building would break so often that the residents would only have to give each other a look when walking in to know exactly what was going on – “stairs”. A crew would come in and “fix it” each time, but they came so frequently I began to recognize their faces. That’s not supposed to happen.
Another example: when a maintenance request was placed and someone finally came to help, it was too often that I’d receive a response along the lines of “Oh no, that’s not a problem”. For example, when we would be discussing important items missing from the oven. All of this, only for them to return and correct themselves, arriving with the missing parts.
Finally, to top it all off, there were gross over charges for supposed “damages”. They racked up a total of $135 worth of move-out fees against me that were proved with images of absolutely nothing on the countertops with a claim for “cleaning charges”. If the image doesn’t show anything wrong, then what could I possibly be paying for? They need to try harder. If they were referring to the speck of dust that formed in the time that we were all moved out and until they finally checked the apartment (3 months later), then I would have become a professional cleaner before I signed a lease with them. Or, I would have come back to Champaign and cleaned it – whatever it was – myself. Not to mention, I let maintenance know about my bathroom cabinet door being broken, but they never helped me out, and in the end they charged me for it.
A final example: there was theft that occurred with packages during my time there. Since the leasing office isn’t located in or anywhere near the building, the packages are carelessly placed just beyond the glass doors, on an open rack, or on the floor. The amenities were also not taken care of, which is hardly ethical because those things were advertised and rationalized as a part of the renting price. The study lounge’s printer never worked, not one day in my less than 9 months of actively living there. The door to the outdoor lounge would not open using the key fob. Finally, the public restroom was never stocked with toiletries.
Overall, I feel that living with The Academy Campustown is not worth the price, nor the amenities. My stay with them was spoiled by the way they attempted to take advantage of myself and other residents. I’m happy to have left.

I lived at the 1008 S 4th St. location during the 2022-23 school year. In the beginning, living in this place was fine. As time went on, the issues seemed never-ending. Let's start with getting a hold of management… practically impossible. When I would call the leasing office (The Dean) most of the time my call would be directed to their off-site answering service. I would be told that someone from the leasing office would call me back, this rarely happened. When I tried to go to their leasing office, they wouldn’t even be there. If I was ever lucky enough to get a hold of someone over the phone, they were often unfriendly before I even mentioned what I was calling for.
Maintenance averages about 2-3 weeks to get to you and often comes unprepared to deal with your request.
The next issue was the elevator (one for the building). It would be broken for a few days every two weeks. Considering the number of times residents had to take the stairs, you would think our fobs would work on the doors to access them. However, the fob would sometimes not work, and you would simply have no access to the rest of the building and your own apartment. I was even locked out of the entire building once since the handle to the front door was broken off. This not only happened to me but also to other residents I have talked to.
The elevator situation got even worse when it broke and remained unfixed around the dates of 5/12-5/18. I moved out May 13th, the Saturday after finals week (a day were a lot of people moved out) and the elevator was, per usual, not working. Myself, and many other residents had no other choice but to move out all their belongings through the stairs. I tried calling the leasing office hoping to get help with this ridiculous situation and surprise, no one answered. When I went in person to speak with them, not only was no one in the office but the wood gate was pulled down clearly indicating no one was working on a day they were supposed to be open. Their website claimed they were open, and the people I spoke to from the off-site answering service insisted that as well. They too, had no idea what to do or what to tell me.
