review_text:
Living at Illini Tower was an experience. If you absolutely cannot stand dorms as a freshman this is about the best you can do. But if you are conflicted here are some things that you don't get to learn until after the leasing process:

Unlike with dorms where you can use your meal card at pretty much any other dining hall, with PCH you can only eat Illini Tower, and their food is consistently not great. At one point the majority of the kitchen staff quit but most residents saw it as a benefit as we were temporarily given credits to visit other, better dining halls.

The fire alarms are incredibly busted at Illini. During winter break a student left their window open, causing pipes to burst and the fire alarm to go on for more than 12 hours(!) and some major water damage. Other than this alarms would erroneously go off during the day, night, during exams, etc. They became so frequent I knew dozens of residents that refused to leave during the alarms because they didn't want to climb upwards of 16 flights of stairs after the all clear was given or wait in the freezing cold for a nonexistent fire.

Elevators are constantly malfunctioning. Don't be surprised if you end up waiting 10 minutes for the elevator to finally hit your floor because 2/4 elevators are down for service. The worst part really is that unless you can somehow find a staff member willing to open the outside stairs doors, you can't go up the stairs. Meaning people on the first floor will be waiting for 5-10 minutes for an elevator when an accessible staircase would get them where they need to go in 30 seconds.

Unless you like to shower at 2am or 6am, don't expect getting hot water. On good days your water may be a few degrees above lukewarm.

Keycards to rooms and getting in the building would often become abruptly unusable and need replaced.

You can only control the A/C, not the heating, so bring some thick blankets for winter.

The amenities are all pretty sad. The gym is consistently dirty and gross, good luck ever getting the movie theatre, there are not enough dryers or washers and students are constantly leaving their laundry in both, and the "music room" is basically a closet with an ancient, untuned piano. The free printing you get means going down to the lobby and hoping there is a staff member there who can print your sheet in the office.

There are some pros to Illini, however. The in-room kitchen is great if you enjoy cooking or want to eat something that actually tastes good. You only have to share your bathroom with up to three other people. It is very close to the main quad and most classes are within easy walking distance. You can stay over breaks and they have an indoor parking lot in the basement for any students that don't want to part with their vehicle. The maintenance staff was great and very nice. However, that's about it.

**** I just wanted to add that Illini Tower suspiciously went from a 3.2/3.1 to nearly four stars in a few weeks. Management is allegedly bribing RAs to meet good reviews. I honestly cannot at all recommend living here.

The worst thing is the noise from upstairs. Since the layout of the rooms is the same and can't even be change，Where I put my bed is also where my upstairs neighbor puts his bed , and any movement he makes to the bed will cause a loud noise. I'm not sure what the source of the noise is, but we're guessing it's the aging of the bed frame, which makes a very harsh sound when the mattress hits the wooden frame. I've been woken up in the middle of the night countless times, including now when I can't sleep because of the awakening, so I'm writing this review. I have tried various ways to solve the problem. I tried to communicate with my neighbor, my neighbor indicated that he had tried his best to tread lightly, but that any contact with the mattress would cause loud noises to be transmitted into my room, including his unconscious rolling motion when he fell asleep. I have also tried to contact the property, but this problem has not been resolved since I moved in last August. Actually, I used to be a morning person, but this room has changed me a lot. In order not to wake up in the middle of the night, I have to wait for my neighbor to fall asleep, which means I usually go to sleep after 3 a.m.The feeling of not being able to control your sleep time is terrible. 4. And I don't feel safe in the neighborhood. Section 8 is right across the street and my friend got mugged in the daylight right in front of the apartment. It's also too far away from the campus.

5. The utilities bill is suspicious. They never send you the details but only send you "hey you owe us $x" When I asked the bill because I needed the detailed utilities bill to prove my residency to another company, the property manager, not a receptionist, told me to directly contact the utility company because they don't know details, although tenants pay bills directly to the apartment. He didn't even tell me which company was, so I had to call Tenants Union to figure out which utility company provides service to the Urbana-Champaign area. I did contact it but the utility company said that they do not have any data because the Pointe pays bills to the company and they have all of the data. The Pointe basically lied to me and I ended up wasting a lot of time. I finally got the detailed bill from another property manager later. Very unpleasant experience.

UPDATE on 9/26/2018: After my husband and I moved out at the end of July 2018, we were told and received written documentation that we were not responsible for any move-out charges. On 9/24/2018, we received an email for a balance on our account for damages incurred on the property, citing a portion of the lease. I called and emailed Jordan Creek, Executive Director of the Pointe at U of I, to inquire where these charges were coming from and stated that I would like an invoice of these damages for my review.

The response I received contained no explanation other than a PDF document with charges for utility overages, not for damages to the property... So, which is it?

There is no consistency at The Pointe at U of I. I feel bad for some of our international neighbors, for whom this is their first experience with American rental properties. This is not how it is supposed to be! Do not move here!

I have advised staff that in the future, when they bill current and previous tenants, to state exactly they're charging for; their current process is not transparent at all and incredibly suspicious. Pointe Staff, be honest, transparent, and accurate with what you're charging for. You'd save yourself and your residents a lot of time and effort.

For those of you with similar experiences, I recommend withholding funds until they can give you the names of the utility companies and account numbers associated with your unit so you can verify whether those charges are accurate. If you incurred damages in your move-out, ask for an itemized invoice of said damages for you to review. Consult legal counsel if necessary- FREE for students at U of I!
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am not a student, but I am married to a U of I Grad student, and we have never had a positive interaction with any of the Pointe Staff Members. Staff are rude, disorganized, and unhelpful. On several occasions, my husband and I have given contact/personal information only to have it lost in their system (whatever that is...). We have requested services (e.g. online portal access- several times, gate key card, etc.) without reply or resolution. Speaking of the parking gate, what exactly are we paying for? This "amenity" has not functioned for nearly 9 months...

Only recently, after living here for a year, did I receive access to be able to pay rent online. We have been good tenants and consistently on time with our monthly dues, however we were late this month. By two days. Rather than have any sort of grace-period, e.g. a day or two, the Pointe at U of I charges a late fee of $26 per resident. They don't care if you're married; they don't care that they haven't given you access to pay your bill online, making you have to hand-deliver checks every month; never mind the fact that their office hours during the summer are shorter, and some of use still work full time jobs; they will charge you $52 for being late. For some people, $52 is a week's worth of groceries or a month's supply of prescription medication. The fact that management is so strict on this policy really baffles me considering the total lack of courtesy and professionalism shown toward their residents. Granted, rental properties are businesses, but it is clear that this organization is only looking for ways to nickel and dime and exploit their residents.

Rest assured, when our lease is up, we will be looking for a new place to live. I do not recommend leasing with this property.

Went to Student Legal Services today. The lawyer literally laughed at the things they charged me. They'll handle it from there.  I don't even have to do much.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Charged me $600 for "damages". When I asked for itemized list, it's actually $400. How shady!

if you don’t want to live so far, don’t want to wait a month for maintenance, and don’t want to be charged blindly, then stay away from the Pointe at U of I.

Don’t bother to try to create an image of a polite and reasonable housing service on Google. Don’t hire people to leave good reviews on Google. I was drawn to 75 Armory because of its very nice interior and layout. Everything seemed like a really good deal when we were signing the lease. Unfortunately, after living here for a year going on my second, I am extremely disappointed with this property.

I won’t lie that the apartment itself is very nice. It’s so nice having a balcony and up to date appliances. I also had a fast response to my maintenance request recently. Management is very nice in person, but lacks communication. A lot of the time they don’t respond to my emails/requests, and I’ve had multiple issues of them saying things that weren’t true.

In the very beginning of last year they told me they would take my mattress because I got a new one. When I called to ask how to go about this they said they couldn’t take it. After some complaining they said the person who said they could take the mattress had been let go. When I contacted them about this through email they were awfully condescending.

Security is always an issue. Most of the time a garage door is open, most of the time you can open the door without a fob. We express our concerns very frequently.

We had an issue with our internet, so I called the office for help. After spending 2 hours total on the phone that day, I finally got the information (not through Next Chapter) that Comcast runs our internet, not Pavlov. This was after the office told me to call Pavlov because they don’t deal with internet. It’s kind of a gamble when you call the office if you’ll talk to someone who knows what they’re doing. I eventually called and someone was VERY helpful in telling me they have a person that specifically helps with internet in 75 Armory. We eventually got out internet fixed after several days without.

So basically if you know who to talk to and have no issues ever this place is right for you. I think it would definitely be worth the price if I felt management actually cared about me as a customer.

review_text:
Haven't moved out yet so can't speak to damages charged after moving out. Skip to bottom for tldr.

Price is relatively high compared to some other apartments, but at a similar tier to other "branded" apartments like the Dean, Seven07, etc. I'd say things are much better compared to what I've heard about the other similar places. Barring mice (see below), everything else has been quite good, no unexpected issues relating to hot water, internet, etc. and it's comfortable. Some people say Octave management doesn't seem to care after you sign, so I was expecting the worst, but actually they seem to be great, in my experience. My roommate and I filed a few different maintenance requests and they've been resolved quickly each time, most importantly. Less importantly, but still nice, the staff as well as the maintenance folks are very friendly. The common rooms downstairs are nice, hallways are good, there's trash disposal on the same room which is convenient, package delivery storage system is solid, etc. No unexpected charges -- just the rent and electricity (well, excluding a one-time $60 utility setup fee, plus whatever else if you need parking or have pets). So I'd say everything is good, have had nothing to complain about and am quite happy with the conveniences and the staff/management... with the exception of mice.

It sounds like many people have reported mice as well. It was fine for us for around 7 or so months, and then in February we had mice for around 6 weeks (though frequently visible/audible only for around 2 of those weeks). Little creatures scurrying around quite fast, makes it hard to sleep and it is kind of startling/uncomfortable to see them around (cute, but unhygenic/unsettling nonetheless). They leave small droppings (though hard to see) which can spread disease, and as you try to remove them, they die in random places, sometimes just in random places on the floor... (if you don't find them, they smell quite strong, which we had to deal with when one died in a glue trap which we didn't find). All of this is quite disturbing, but considering the other 8.5/10 months have been perfectly good, I'm willing to give a pass on this, especially now that it's over. My experience with the front desk/management in relation to this has been quite good, they were quick to relay stuff to the pest control, file maintenance reports related to the mice for us, and pest control comes to place traps and remove the traps for you (glue traps or rodenticide), and clean up any dead mice if you don't want to touch them (front office will do so as well). Though pest control can have around 2-5 days response time, it seems to me like the management is genuinely trying their best (though it's also somewhat the case that "their best is not enough", since mice are a very significant issue...).

Long story short(er), 4 stars since I'm very happy with the conveniences (common rooms, trash disposal, package storage system, general niceness of interior), no unexpected issues (except mice, for a shortish period of time), and management/front desk/maintenance seem genuinely very helpful/friendly, in my experience. However, a very unsettling issue of mice, for a period of 2-6 weeks -- the management is quick to address these, but it is disturbing nonetheless. I'd say the rest of the factors offset this enough that I'd give it 4 stars (generally speaking without the mice everything is great imo). Pray you don't get mice, and otherwise, if you're looking for an apartment around this price range I would recommend (also, I hear people can get very significant discounts on their first year of rent if you get a huge group together like 50 or so people, lol).

review_text: I do not recommend living at 309 Green. Over this year, I've dealt with many inconveniences. For example, the first day I moved in after all the rooms had supposedly been "cleaned" and ready for move in, my dad and I stepped foot in my apartment and he refused to accept it the way it was. There was dirt, dust, and hair all over the floors, drawers and cabinets... and not to mention cigarette burns in the cloth couch I had initially which was then swapped for a leather one. They had to get a maintenance crew and reclean it for a few hours. Also, when it starts getting warmer, the fitness center is always extremely hot. I don't think they turned the AC on upon move in for 3-4 weeks even throughout my complains to the front desk who always assured me they were working on it. Also, the elevators are either broken or slow. During move in week, you have no choice but to take the stairs because an elevator can take up to 15 minutes. Next, the light bulbs in the rooms burn out every 2-3 weeks which is annoying to have to call to get them replaced so often. Also, the outdoor amenities are very poor. The hot tub never opened last fall and the pool was always freezing. This spring, 309 decided to start exterior renovations a little before finals week which meant loud drilling outside your balcony from 8-5 am which made it impossible to study. During this time, our balconies got locked so we could not enjoy the nice weather during our last weeks at 309. Also, there is a $250 subleasing fee if someone who lives here decides to let someone else live here for the summer. One of my roommates had done everything right and got a money order for $250 giving it to the staff back in November, anticipating she would be subleasing, and towards the end of the semester the staff had informed her they never received her money and suggested she pay them again after it was THEIR mistake for losing the money. Anyone who lives in the 309  apartments will have a similar experience to me and the other negative reviews on this page (besides the good reviews in which the people received $10 for writing). As for renovations, maybe they should shift their focus on issues their residents care about such as the fixing the hot tub or adding another elevator since everyone here pays good money for the amenities. Over all, I do not recommend this place and will definitely be living across the street at the Here apartments for the same price and far better amenities.

review_text: I've been living in 309 for a half year. So far I quite enjoy my experience here. I like their package-checking system at the front desk. They have a lock-secured mail room to keep all incoming packages and requires your ID & signature to receive. The system send me reminder email when a package is arrived, signed or hasn't been picked up in 3 days upon arrival. For a person who used to shop online often like me, it's great that I never have to worry about losing packages or forgetting to sign. Staffs are always very patient and helpful. They always answer my questions and address my concerns well. The maintenance is very efficient. They come and fix promptly within 1 day after submitting an online work order.

I definitely regret choosing to live in 309. For the amount of money you're paying, there are definitely much better options. For one, the amenities aren't all they crack up to be. The hot tub never opened, the pool was open for maybe three weeks in the fall, and you have to bring your own paper for the free printer. One of the elevators is almost always broken, and for a building of this size that means it could easily take 10 minutes to catch an elevator sometimes. The staff randomly walks into your apartment, one time a worker walked into my personal bedroom saying he was "just checking to make sure the key worked to my bedroom." Now worst of all, they locked our balcony doors weeks ago and have yet to unlock them because of "construction on the outside of the building," which there has been very little of. The school year ends in a few weeks, so I won't even get to spend the nicest weeks of the spring on my balcony. Additionally, the room furnishings are inconsistent. My apartment has leather couches with kitchen stools with backs on them, while other apartments in this building have cloth couches and steel stools, which seems unfair. Also, there is a giant concrete pole running through our kitchen that we were not told ahead of time would be in our apartment. The apartment we were shown when considering the apartment is nothing like the apartment we got. The staff is friendly, the location is nice, the parking is convenient (but expensive,) so it isn't all bad, but I personally think if you're going to spend $800 a month, there a much better options in Champaign.

Also, the reason there are so many positive reviews in a row on this page is because the staff offered $10 gift cards to anyone who left a review. I'd be wary to trust all of them.
